positiveFlows.title: THE MISSION OF THE SOUTHERN IPM CENTER (SIPMC) IS TO FOSTER DEVELOPMENT AND ADOPTION OF INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM), A SCIENCE-BASED APPROACH TO MANAGING PESTS IN WAYS THAT GENERATE ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL AND HUMAN HEALTH BENEFITS. SIPMC'S UNIQUE STRENGTHS WILL BE LEVERAGED THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG THREE SOUTHERN INSTITUTIONS (NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY, UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA, AND AUBURN UNIVERSITY) IN PARTNERSHIP WITH REGIONAL STAKEHOLDERS IN MULTIPLE SECTORS FROM AGRICULTURAL, URBAN, AND RURAL SETTINGS TO IDENTIFY AND ADDRESS REGIONAL PRIORITIES FOR RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND OUTREACH. ADDITIONAL SUPPORT AND DIRECTION HAS BEEN PROVIDED SO THAT SIPMC ALSO MANAGES A RICH PORTFOLIO OF APPLICATIONS AND EXPERTISE THAT SERVE AS THE FOUNDATION FOR THE IPM INFORMATION SUPPLEMENT. INCLUDED IN OUR CURRENT PROPOSAL ARE PROGRAMS THAT NOT ONLY SATISFY MULTIPLE PRIORITIES OF THE CROP PROTECTION AND PEST MANAGEMENT PROGRAM, BUT ALSO PROMOTE THE FIVE GOALS OF THE NATIONAL IPM ROADMAP. THESE INCLUDE 1) IMPROVED IPM PRACTICES THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PROGRAMS: REGULATORY SCIENCE NETWORK, FACILITATION OF INNOVATION THROUGH TECHNOLOGY (FITT), POLLINATOR PROTECTION, RESISTANCE MANAGEMENT, NATIONAL IPM DATABASE, AND GRANT PROGRAMS 2) ECONOMICAL IPM PRACTICES THROUGH FITT, INVASIVE SPECIES, RESISTANCE MANAGEMENT, NATIONAL IPM DATABASE, GRANT PROGRAMS, AND UNDERSERVED AUDIENCES 3) REDUCED ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS THROUGH FITT, INVASIVE SPECIES, GRANT PROGRAMS, RESISTANCE MANAGEMENT, AND UNDERSERVED AUDIENCES. 4) INCREASED IPM ADOPTION: FITT, INVASIVE SPECIES, REGULATORY SCIENCE NETWORK, GRANT PROGRAMS, EVALUATION AND COMMUNICATION, NATIONAL IPM DATABASE, FRIENDS OF SOUTHERN IPM AWARDS, AND UNDERSERVED AUDIENCES, AND FINALLY, 5) REDUCED HUMAN HEALTH RISKS THROUGH FITT, REGULATORY SCIENCE NETWORK, POLLINATOR PROTECTION, GRANT PROGRAMS, AND UNDERSERVED AUDIENCES.

THE NORTHEASTERN IPM CENTER, BY TAKING BOLD AND INNOVATIVE STEPS, WILL STRENGTHEN TIES TO STAKEHOLDERS IN THE REGION AND FINE-TUNE OPERATIONS TO FULFILL ITS MISSION OF FOSTERING THE DEVELOPMENT AND ADOPTION OF IPM IN THE REGION. STAFF, IN COLLABORATION WITH STATE IPM PARTNERS,MULTIREGIONAL PROJECTS, OUR ADVISORY COUNCIL, SCIENTISTS, AND IPM PRACTITIONERS, WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES, DIVERSIFY RESOURCES, AND PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR OUR CLIENTELE. FIVE SIGNATURE PROGRAMS EMBRACE ALL CENTER ACTIVITIES: IPM IN ORGANIC SYSTEMS, CLIMATE CHANGE AND EMERGING PESTS, URBAN TO RURAL IPM, NEXT GENERATION EDUCATION, AND ADVANCED PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. IN ADDITION, THE CENTER WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE OTHER CENTERS TO FOCUS ON ADDRESSING INVASIVE SPECIES INCLUDING THE NEWLY EMERGING SPOTTED LANTERNFLY. THE CENTER WILL SERVE AS A HUB FOR DELIVERING HIGH QUALITY INFORMATION TO STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING UNDERSERVED AUDIENCES. WE WILL COLLABORATE WITH OTHER GROUPS TO OFFER AN ANNUAL ONLINE IPM CONFERENCE, A SERIES OF IPM TOOLBOX WEBINARS WITH PRACTICAL IPM TOOLS FOR USE IN THE FIELD, AND TRANSITION OUR QUARTERLY PRINT PUBLICATION, INSIGHTS, TO AN ONLINE FORMAT. THE CENTER WILL COMMUNICATE SUCCESSES GENERATED BY THE IPM PARTNERSHIP GRANTS PROGRAM, WHICH WILL FUND REGIONAL WORKING GROUPS, RESEARCH AND EXTENSION WORK, AND COMMUNICATION PROJECTS. ALL PROJECTS, INTERNAL OR EXTERNAL, WILL BE DESIGNED TO MAXIMIZE EVALUATION AND ENSURE IMPACT. FUNDING WILL SUPPORT DIVERSE PROGRAMMING ON IPM AND ENHANCE THE CENTER'S CAPACITY TO LEVERAGE ADDITIONAL FUNDS TO ADVANCE THE MISSION TO IMPLEMENT IPM IN A WIDER GEOGRAPHIC AND DEMOGRAPHIC CIRCLE.

THE WESTERN INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT CENTER'S VISION - OUR STATEMENT OF THE FUTURE OUTCOME WE ARE WORKING TO ACHIEVE - IS "A HEALTHIER WEST WITH FEWER PESTS." THIS IS THE GOAL WE'RE WORKING TOWARD AND THE IMPACT WE'RE PURSUING FOR THE PEOPLE OF THE AMERICAN WEST. WE BELIEVE THAT WIDESPREAD IPM ADOPTION WILL REALIZE THAT VISION, AND THE KEYS TO ACHIEVING THAT LEVEL OF ADOPTION ARE IMPROVED IPM SYSTEMS AND IMPROVED AREAWIDE IPM APPROACHES. WE SUPPORT THOSE KEY AREAS THROUGH A GRANT-FUNDING PROGRAM AND COLLABORATIVE SIGNATURE PROGRAMS TO DEVELOP THE SCIENCE AND DELIVER ACTIONABLE RESULTS TO PEST MANAGERS; BY BUILDING, EXPANDING AND LEADING PARTNERSHIPS WITHIN AND BEYOND THE REGION TO EXPAND IPM AWARENESS AND INTEGRATION INTO OTHER SYSTEMS; AND BY SERVING AS AN INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS HUB FOR THE IPM COMMUNITY THROUGHOUT THE WEST TO IMPROVE COOPERATION, COLLABORATION AND AREAWIDE INTEGRATION OF PROGRAMS AND EFFORTS.THIS PROJECT CONTINUES THE WESTERN IPM CENTER, SUPPORTING THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE'S NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE'S CROP PROTECTION AND PEST MANAGEMENT PROGRAM GOAL OF ADDRESSING HIGH PRIORITY PEST ISSUES THROUGH REGIONAL IPM AND ALL CROP PROTECTION AND PEST MANAGEMENT FOCUS AREAS: PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS, ENHANCING AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY, AND IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES. OUR GOALS ARE TO REDUCE RISKS TO PEOPLE AND THE ENVIRONMENT FROM PESTS AND PEST-MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, AND TO IMPROVE THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF ADOPTING IPM. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE (1) CREATING IPM KNOWLEDGE, TOOLS AND RESOURCES BY FUNDING IPM RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECTS REGIONALLY; LEADING EFFORTS TO INCORPORATE RISK ASSESSMENT INTO IPM DECISION MAKING; SUPPORTING STATES IN COMBATTING INVASIVE SPECIES; (2) COORDINATING IPM EFFORTS ACROSS BORDERS AND BOUNDARIES BY SERVING AS A REGIONAL HUB FOR IPM INFORMATION AND RESOURCES; AND REPRESENTING THE WEST IN NATIONAL EFFORTS AND PROGRAMS; ENGAGE OTHER PROGRAMS TO INTEGRATE IPM INTO RELATED EFFORTS AND SYSTEMS; (3) COMMUNICATING IPM SUCCESSES AND STAKEHOLDER NEEDS BY SUPPORTING AND AMPLIFYING STATE IPM EFFORTS BY COMMUNICATING SUCCESSES WIDELY; INFORMING POLICIES BY PROVIDING RELEVANT FACTS TO POLICYMAKERS; AND IMPROVING REGULATIONS BY PROVIDING GROWER AND USE DATA; AND (4) EVALUATING IPM IMPACTS, ECONOMICS AND PROGRAMS BY SUPPORTING ASSESSMENT EFFORTS AND TOOLS, INCLUDING CROP-PEST LOSS SURVEYS AND THE ASSESSMENT TOOLKIT; SUPPORTING AND ASSISTING STATE IPM PROGRAMS WITH EVALUATIONS; AND COLLECTING AND ANALYZING DATA TO DOCUMENT IPM IMPACTS AND NEEDS.OUR WORK AND VISION ARE LONG TERM BUT BUILT ON SHORT-TERM PROJECTS AND CYCLES. OUR CURRENT PROGRAM CONTINUES TO BUILD THE SCIENTIFIC STRUCTURES TO IMPROVE PEST MANAGEMENT WHILE PROTECTING FARMERS' PROFITABILITY AND HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH. ONE SPECIFIC WAY OUR WORK ACCOMPLISHES THIS IS BY SUPPORTING RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AIMED AT REDUCING PESTICIDE USE. WE HAVE INVESTED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF ACCURATE, REAL-WORLD DATA ON CROP PEST LOSSES AND PESTICIDE USE. THESE DATA SHOW THAT WHEN GROWERS ADOPT IPM, THEIR PESTICIDE USE IS REDUCED. OUR RESEARCH ON IPM ADOPTION CONFIRMS THIS AND SHOWS THAT EVEN WHEN GROWERS PRODUCE HIGH-VALUE COMMODITIES, AN IPM PROGRAM RESULTS IN LOWER OVERALL PESTICIDE USE AND OFTEN FEWER PESTICIDE APPLICATIONS. OUR CENTER IS CONTINUALLY INVESTING IN RESEARCH ON BETTER IPM PRACTICES, ON OUTREACH TO GROWERS SO THEY ADOPT THOSE NEW PRACTICES, AND ON EVALUATION TO CLOSE THE LOOP AND MEASURE THE IMPACT OF IPM ADOPTION. THIS CYCLE OF NEW KNOWLEDGE LEADING TO NEW ACTION LEADING TO NEW CONDITIONS WILL CREATE THE POSITIVE SOCIETAL IMPACTS OF INCREASING ECONOMIC HEALTH FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS WHILE REDUCING RISKS TO HUMAN HEALTH AND PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, IN OTHER WORDS, A HEALTHIER WEST WITH FEWER PESTS.

THE CONTINUING RISE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF HERBICIDE-RESISTANT WEEDS DRIVES THE NEED FOR INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT (IWM) TACTICS TO PRESERVE CROP YIELDS AND MAKE MORE JUDICIOUS USE OF HERBICIDES. THE USE OF COVER CROPS IS ONE TOOL IN THE IWM ARSENAL. HOWEVER, IWM IN GENERAL AND THE USE OF COVER CROPS SPECIFICALLY HAVE NOT BEEN WIDELY ADOPTED, LARGELY BECAUSE THE COMPLEXITY OF INTERACTIONS AMONG COVER CROPS, CLIMATE, SOIL, MANAGEMENT, AND WEEDS IS DAUNTING AND MAKES IWM A TIME-CONSUMING TASK. WE PROPOSE ON-FARM RESEARCH AT MANY SITES ACROSS A WIDE LATITUDINAL GRADIENT TO DEFINE AND COVER CROP MANAGEMENT BY ENVIRONMENT IMPACTS ON WEEDS TO IMPROVE THE PRECISION OF COVER CROPS AS AN IWM TOOL BY CREATING LITERAL MANAGEMENT IWM DECISION TOOLS THAT REDUCE COMPLEXITY FOR FARMERS. IN DOING SO WE AIM TO INCREASE THE ADOPTION OF COVER CROPS AS AN IWM PRACTICE AND TO IMPROVE THE USE OF IWM IN GENERAL BY MAKING IT EASIER FOR FARMERS TO TARGET (AND THUS REDUCE) HERBICIDE APPLICATIONS WHILE REALIZING ANCILLARY BENEFITS OF COVER CROPS (E.G. REDUCED SOIL EROSION, NUTRIENT LOSS, ETC.). THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS THE ULTIMATE CPPM GOAL OF SUSTAINABLE FOOD SECURITY THROUGH THE IMPROVEMENT OF IWM PRACTICES (I.E. INCLUSION OF COVER CROPS IN CROPPING SYSTEMS TO MANAGE WEEDS) THAT INCREASES IPM ADOPTION (I.E. USE OF NON-HERBICIDE METHODS OF WEED CONTROL) AND REDUCES ENVIRONMENTAL AND HUMAN HEALTH RISKS (I.E. VIA DECREASED HERBICIDE APPLICATION) WHILE SUPPORTING FARMER PROFITABILITY.

THERE HAVE BEEN IMPORTANT RECENT ADVANCES IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TO CONTROL THE PRIORITY PEST CONCERNS FOR REGIONAL BLUEBERRY GROWERS, OFFERING POTENTIAL ALTERNATIVES TO THE CURRENT HIGH RATES OF INSECTICIDE APPLICATIONS THAT ARE FOCUSED ON KEY PESTS INCLUDING GALL WASP AND SPOTTED WING DROSOPHILA. WE WILL EVALUATE AND DEMONSTRATE EFFECTIVE IPM PROGRAMS, WHILE ALSO COMPARING THE RETURN ON INVESTMENT OF DIFFERENT APPROACHES. USE OF SCOUTING AND DEGREE-DAY MODELS IS EXPECTED TO BETTER INFORM SPRAY PROGRAM INITIATION, ALLOW LONGER SPRAY INTERVALS, AND ALLOW TARGETED SPRAYING ON AREAS OF THE FARM. ADDITIONALLY, MULCHING AND PRUNING HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO REDUCE PEST INFESTATION AND THEY WILL BE TESTED IN COMBINATION WITH REDUCED-RISK INSECTICIDE PROGRAMS. CONSERVATION BIOLOGICAL CONTROL AND TARGETED USE OF NEMATODES ALSO SHOW PROMISE FOR REGULATING PEST LEVELS BELOW ECONOMIC THRESHOLDS. WE WILL EVALUATE THESE APPROACHES AT COMMERCIAL BLUEBERRY FARMS TO DETERMINE THEIR POTENTIAL FOR IMPROVING FRUIT QUALITY, REDUCING PESTICIDE COSTS, AND LOWERING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT AND WORKER RISK. SINCE ECONOMICS IS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF IPM ADOPTION, THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO COMPARE THE COSTS AND BENEFITS OF DIFFERENT IPM COMPONENTS TO HIGHLIGHT THEIR RETURN-ON-INVESTMENT. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO OUR EXISTING BILINGUAL EXTENSION PROGRAMMING TO ADVANCE THE GOALS OF THE CPPM PROGRAM.

BROWN STINK BUG, EUSCHISTUS SERVUS, IS THE COSTLIEST AND MOST PROBLEMATIC INSECT PEST OF CORN IN THE SOUTHEASTERN US, AND A MAJOR PEST OF SOYBEAN AND COTTON ACROSS THE SOUTHERN US. SOME EARLY SEASON HOSTS, OVERWINTERING LOCATION, AND THE ASSOCIATION OF PREVIOUS YEAR'S SOYBEANS TO BROWN STINK BUG PREVALENCE IN CORN ARE KNOWN, BUT THESE FACTORS HAVE NEVER BEEN HOLISTICALLY STUDIED TO SEE IF THEY ARE LINKED. WE PROPOSE SUCH A STUDY TO BETTER IDENTIFY CORN FIELDS AT RISK FOR BROWN STINK BUG. WE WILL: 1) MEASURE STINK BUG POPULATIONS IN SUITABLE HOST CROPS DURING THE AUTUMN WHERE CORN WILL BE PLANTED DURING THE SPRING; 2) CHARACTERIZE OVERWINTERING HABITATS BASED ON THE CATEGORIZATION OF HOST PLANTS OR FOREST STRUCTURE; 3) MEASURE BROWN STINK BUG COLONIZATION INTO SPRING CORN ADJACENT TO NON-CROP OVERWINTERING HABITATS AND ANNUAL CROPS; 4) ESTIMATE STINK BUG INJURY IN FOCAL CORN FIELDS; 5) ASSESS CORN YIELDS RELATIVE TO STINK BUG DENSITY AND LANDSCAPE FEATURES; 6) IDENTIFY LANDSCAPES AT RISK FOR INFESTATION BY BROWN STINK BUG AND CREATE A RISK MAP FOR THE SOUTHEASTERN US; AND 7) DOCUMENT BASELINES FOR MANAGEMENT OF BROWN STINK BUG IN FIELD CROPS AND DISSEMINATE BROWN STINK BUG RISK MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATION TO RELEVANT STAKEHOLDERS. WE HOPE THAT BY DOCUMENTING THE SOURCE-SINK DYNAMICS OF BROWN STINK BUG AMONG YEARS THAT WE WILL IDENTIFY KEY COMBINATIONS OF CROPS AND NON-CROP OVERWINTERING HABITATS THAT ELEVATE RISK FOR BROWN STINK BUG COLONIZATION. THIS WILL LEAD TO MORE SCOUTING FOR BROWN STINK BUG IN THE CORRECT PLACES.

THIS IS AN ARDP RESEARCH (SINGLE-FUNCTION) MULTI-STATE, MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL PROJECT THAT AIMS TO IMPROVE ADOPTION OF PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS (A) BY DEMONSTRATING HOW LONG-LASTING INSECTICIDE-INCORPORATED NETTING (LLIN) MAY SYNERGIZE EFFICACY OF PEST MANAGEMENT WHEN USED WITH A DIVERSIFIED SUITE OF OTHER MANAGEMENT TACTICS AT FOOD FACILITIES IN THE US. THIS IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT WITH THE LOSS OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FUMIGANT IN POSTPHARVEST PEST MANAGEMENT, METHYL BROMIDE, AS WELL AS INCREASING CHALLENGES WITH THE USE OF THE MOST COMMON REPLACEMENT, PHOSPHINE, INCLUDING WIDESPREAD DEVELOPMENT OF RESISTANCE AND INCREASING DEMAND BY END CONSUMERS FOR FEWER CHEMICAL INPUTS. OUR TEAM HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT LLIN IS EFFECTIVE, LONG-LASTING, AND CONFINES INSECTICIDE USE TO THE NETTING AND AWAY FROM THE COMMODITY. HOWEVER, WE PROPOSE TO SPEED ADOPTION BY 1) SYNERGIZING LLIN DEPLOYMENT TO IMPROVE PHOSPHINE FUMIGATION EFFICACY, 2) DEMONSTRATING COMPATIBILITY OF LLIN WITH AEROSOL USE, 3) IMPROVING MANAGEMENT OUTCOMES OF USING A NOVEL RESIDUAL CONTACT INSECTICIDE BY PAIRING WITH LLIN, AND 4) DEVELOPING ONLINE RESOURCES FOR STAKEHOLDERS AND ASSESSING ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY OF INCORPORATING LLIN INTO MANAGEMENT. OUR PROJECT COVERS THE MOST COMMON PEST MANAGEMENT TACTICS USED AT FOOD FACILITIES, AND SHOULD DEMONSTRATE THAT LLIN IS NOT JUST COMPATIBLE WITH EXISTING IPM PROGRAMS, BUT WILL VASTLY IMPROVE THEIR EFFICACY. IN TURN, THIS WILL SPEED TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER AND ADOPTION OF LLIN TECHNOLOGY BY FOOD FACILITIES. OUR PROPOSAL INCLUDES PERSONNEL REPRESENTING KANSAS, NEBRASKA, AND ARKANSAS, AND WILL THUS HELP PROTECT THE US'S ROLE AS THE BREADBASKET OF THE WORLD, SUPPORTING USDA STRATEGIC GOAL 2.

FIRE BLIGHT IS RANKED BY THE U.S. APPLE GROWERS AS THE MOST CONCERNING POME FRUIT DISEASE, WITH ANNUAL ECONOMIC LOSSES AND COSTS OF DISEASE CONTROL ESTIMATED OVER $100 MILLION NATIONWIDE. DUE TO THE LACK OF EFFECTIVE CULTURAL CONTROL, THE MANAGEMENT OF THE FIRE BLIGHT DISEASE RELIES HEAVILY ON ANTIBIOTIC STREPTOMYCIN. HOWEVER, THE LONG-TERM USE OF STREPTOMYCIN HAS FACILITATED THE PATHOGEN TO DEVELOP RESISTANCE. SINCE THE INITIAL REPORT IN 1971, STREPTOMYCIN RESISTANCE HAS BEEN CONSTANTLY OBSERVED IN ALMOST ALL APPLE-PRODUCING REGIONS IN THE U.S. THE CONTINUED USE OF THE ANTIBIOTIC STREPTOMYCIN, ALBEIT BECOMING LESS EFFICIENT, NOT ONLY RESULTED IN CATASTROPHIC LOSSES OF CROPS AND TREES DUE TO FAILURES IN CONTROLLING THE DISEASE BUT ALSO IMPOSES A THREAT TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN HEALTH.INSTEAD OF AIMING TO KILL THE PATHOGEN WITH ANTIBIOTICS WHICH FACILITATED THE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE DEVELOPMENT, ANOTHER DISEASE CONTROL STRATEGY IS TO INHIBIT THE VIRULENCE OF THE PATHOGEN. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDY, WE IDENTIFIED A SERIES OF SMALL PHENOLIC COMPOUNDS THAT CAN INHIBIT THE EXPRESSION OF KEY VIRULENCE GENES IN THE FIRE BLIGHT PATHOGEN E. AMYLOVORA. WHILE SUCH COMPOUNDS EFFECTIVELY REPRESS THE VIRULENCE OF E. AMYLOVORA, IT HOWEVER DOES NOT AFFECT BACTERIAL SURVIVAL AND GROWTH. WE PROVED THAT SUPPRESSING SUCH VIRULENCE USING VIS COULD POTENTIALLY LEAD TO EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF THE FIRE BLIGHT DISEASE. WE BELIEVE THAT THE VIS CAN PROVIDE A MORE SUSTAINABLE APPROACH IN CONTROLLING FIRE BLIGHT, AS THE VIS DO NOT IMPOSE SELECTIVE PRESSURE ON THE PATHOGEN, THERE IS LESS CHANCE FOR THEM TO MUTATE AND DEVELOP RESISTANCE TO THE VIRULENCE INHIBITORS AS THE ANTIBIOTICS DO. IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL FIELD APPLICATION CONDITIONS AND EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF THE VIS TO THE ENVIRONMENT. WE AIM TO INCREASE GROWERS' AWARENESS OF THIS NEW STRATEGY AND POTENTIAL BENEFITS. OUR ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP FOR FARMERS THIS NEW MANAGEMENT TOOL AS A VIABLE, COST-EFFICIENT, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY ALTERNATIVE TO THE USE OF ANTIBIOTICS IN AGRICULTURAL DISEASE MANAGEMENT.

NEW CONTROL OPTIONS FOR HERBICIDE-RESISTANT BARNYARDGRASS AND PALMER AMARANTH WERE LISTED AS THE MOST IMPORTANT RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL NEED IN RICE BY MID-SOUTH STAKEHOLDERS. THE INCREASE IN GLOBAL DEMAND FOR RICE AND NEWLY UTILIZED PRODUCTION PRACTICES (FURROW-IRRIGATED RATHER THAN FLOODED) REQUIRE GREATER PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY AND A HOLISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE CROPPING SYSTEM. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR IDENTIFICATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT (IWM) TACTICS, INCLUDING CULTURAL STRATEGIES (SUCH AS MANIPULATING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF THE CROP THROUGH ALTERATIONS TO DRILL SPACING) AND OPTIMIZATION OF CHEMICAL CONTROL METHODS (ACHIEVING GREATER SPRAY COVERAGE WHILE REDUCING OFF-TARGET MOVEMENT AND THE NUMBER OF REQUIRED APPLICATIONS), TO BETTER MANAGE WEEDS IN RICE ACROSS THE MID-SOUTH REGION. OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP EFFECTIVE IWM STRATEGIES UTILIZING DRILL SPACING AND BED WIDTH (SPACING BETWEEN IRRIGATION FURROWS) MANIPULATION, AND HERBICIDE APPLICATION OPTIMIZATION THROUGH PROPER NOZZLE SELECTION (DROPLET SIZE, SPRAY ANGLE, ETC.) IN COORDINATION WITH THESE CULTURAL STRATEGIES, TO MORE EFFECTIVELY MANAGE WEEDS WHILE REDUCING INPUTS, THEREBY IMPROVING PROFITABILITY AND EFFICIENCY OF RICE PRODUCERS IN BOTH FLOODED AND FURROW-IRRIGATED RICE. FLOODED RICE IS MOST COMMONLY UTILIZED AS IT PROVIDES THE NECESSARY IRRIGATION TO A DROUGHT-SENSITIVE CROP LIKE RICE, WHILE ALSO PROVIDING A CULTURAL WEED MANAGEMENT TOOL TO REDUCE WEEDS THAT CAN'T SURVIVE IN A FLOODED ENVIRONMENT. HOWEVER, THE REQUIREMENTS TO BUILD LEVEES TO SUSTAIN A FLOODED ENVIRONMENT IS VERY LABOR INTENSIVE AND REQUIRES A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF TILLAGE. FURROW-IRRIGATED RICE ALLEVIATES THESE CHALLENGES BY ELIMINATING THE NEED FOR LEVEES, THEREBY SAVING LABOR COSTS AS WELL AS BEING MORE ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY THROUGH REDUCED TILLAGE, FUEL CONSUMPTION, AND METHANE EMISSIONS AS COMPARED TO FLOODED RICE, BUT CREATES NEW CHALLENGES FOR WEED MANAGEMENT. OUR SPECIFIC AIM IS TO CONDUCT FIELD STUDIES EVALUATING THE EFFECT OF DRILL SPACING, BED WIDTH, AND NOZZLE TYPE ON: (1) HERBICIDE-RESISTANT BARNYARDGRASS AND PALMER AMARANTH CONTROL, GROWTH, AND SEED PRODUCTION, (2) HERBICIDE SPRAY COVERAGE, AND (3) RICE LODGING AND YIELD IN FLOODED AND FURROW-IRRIGATED PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. DISSEMINATION OF RESULTS AND RECOMMENDATIONS THROUGH MULTIPLE EXTENSION SOURCES (PUBLICATIONS, ONLINE VIDEOS, DIRECT TEXT MESSAGES, COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS) TO INCREASE ADOPTION OF IWM STRATEGIES IN RICE WILL BE PRIORITIZED TO DIVERSIFY WEED MANAGEMENT TACTICS, MITIGATE HERBICIDE RESISTANCE EVOLUTION, AND INCREASE PRODUCER PROFITABILITY. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL HELP INCREASE AWARENESS OF U.S. RICE SUSTAINABILITY. BY INCREASING WEED CONTROL THROUGH SUSTAINABLE MEANS, REDUCTIONS IN WEED SEEDS IN GRAIN CAN BE ATTAINED TO INCREASE EXPORT ACCEPTANCE AND BENEFIT THE NATIONAL ECONOMY. THIS PROJECT WILL ASSIST IN THE CREATION OF A KNOWLEDGEABLE AND COMPETITIVE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE (UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS, FARMERS, CROP CONSULTANTS, AND MANY OTHERS). FINALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE THE RESOLVE OF U.S. RICE PRODUCERS TO PROVIDE A SUSTAINABLE, SAFE, AND HIGH-QUALITY FOOD PRODUCT THAT CAN BE ENJOYED INTERNATIONALLY.

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE APHID METOPOLOPHIUM FESTUCAE CEREALIUM (MFC) HAS EMERGED OVER THE LAST SEVERAL YEARS AS ONE OF THE MOST ABUNDANT APHIDS PRESENT IN WHEAT SYSTEMS OF NORTHERN IDAHO, WASHINGTON, AND NORTHERN OREGON. MFC CAUSES A CHLOROTIC REACTION IN WHEAT AND OTHER GRASSES, SUGGESTING IT IS ESPECIALLY INJURIOUS. THUS, WHEAT SYSTEMS THAT ACCOUNT FOR AS MUCH AS 18% OF PRODUCTION IN THE USA ARE POTENTIALLY AFFECTED. TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE, THIS PROJECT HAS THREE OBJECTIVES: 1. ASSESS THE EXTENT AND DIVERSITY OF MFC INFESTATIONS IN WHEAT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES, 2. DETERMINE THE EXTENT OF MFC DAMAGE AND DEVELOP MANAGEMENT THRESHOLDS, AND 3. DEVELOP NOVEL APHID IDENTIFICATION AND DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS FOR PRODUCERS. OBJECTIVE 1 WILL DELINEATE MFC PRESENCE IN WHEAT AND NON-CULTIVATED PERENNIAL GRASS HOSTS AND DOCUMENT EXPANSION INTO OTHER STATES, ASSESS THE GENETIC DIVERSITY AND PROJECT THE POTENTIAL GEOGRAPHIC RANGE OF MFC IN NORTH AMERICA. TO DEVELOP MANAGEMENT THRESHOLDS, OBJECTIVE 2 WILL EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL ROLE OF MFC AS A VIRUS VECTOR AND QUANTIFY DIRECT FEEDING DAMAGE. THE EXTENSION COMPONENT OF THE PROJECT (OBJECTIVE 3) WILL DEVELOP ONLINE DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS FOR INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF CEREAL APHIDS, INCLUDING MFC, WHICH WILL ENTAIL >20% OF TOTAL PROJECT EFFORT. PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL ADDRESS TWO CPPM GOALS: IMPROVED INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) PRACTICES, INCREASED IPM ADOPTION.

positiveFlows.title: THE DIAMONDBACK MOTH, PLUTELLA XYLOSTELLA, IS A NOTORIOUS PEST OF COLE AND OTHER BRASSICA CROPS. IT IS ALSO KNOWN FOR THE RAPID EVOLUTION OF RESISTANCE TO INSECTICIDES, AND IS LIKELY RESISTANT TO A BROADER ARRAY OF INSECTICIDES THAN ANY OTHER CROP PEST. IN THE SOUTHEASTERN USA, THIS HAS LED TO FREQUENT CONTROL FAILURES AND ASSOCIATED LOSS OF REVENUE FOR GROWERS. IN THE PREVIOUS CYCLE, WE DEVELOPED A MAXIMUM DOSE ASSAY TO ASSIST GROWERS IN PLANNING INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS. THIS ASSAY EXPOSES LARVAE TO THE MAXIMUM LABELED DOSE OF A VARIETY OF INSECTICIDES; IF LARVAE SURVIVE THE EXPOSURE IN SIGNIFICANT NUMBERS USE OF THE INSECTICIDE IS COUNTER-INDICATED. A CONSTRAINT OF THE ASSAY IS THE NEED FOR A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF LARVAE. THE CURRENT STUDY SEEKS TO DEVELOP GENETIC TOOLS, PARTICULARLY QUANTITATIVE PCR ASSAYS, TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE OF ALLELES (OR MUTATIONS) ASSOCIATED WITH RESISTANCE, INITIALLY TO CHLORANTRANILIPROLE (CORAGEN) AND LATER TO OTHER INSECTICIDES. IDEALLY THESE ASSAYSCAN BE RAPID AND WORK WITH SMALLER SAMPLE SIZES OF LARVAE, OR WITH ADULTS CAUGHT ON PHEROMONE TRAPS, PROVIDING TIMELY INFORMATION TO GROWERS PLANNING THEIR INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS.INITIALLY WE WILL FOCUS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC PCR ASSAYS TO QUANTIFY THE PROPORTION OF SUSCEPTIBLE AND RESISTANT ALLELES IN FIELD POPULATIONS. COMPARISON OF THE RESULTS WITH BIOASSAY RESULTS FROM THE SAME POPULATIONS WILL ALLOW US TO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL RELATING ALLELE FREQUENCY TO THE LIKELIHOOD OF CONTROL FAILURE. positiveFlows.title: BRETZIELLA FAGACEARUM IS A FUNGAL PLANT PATHOGEN THAT CAUSES OAK WILT DISEASE IN MANY ECOLOGICALLY AND ECONOMICALLY IMPORTANT OAK TREE SPECIES. SYMPTOMS OF OAK WILT ARE EASILY CONFUSED WITH DROUGHT STRESS AND OTHER BACTERIAL DISEASES THAT ARE VECTORED BY INSECT LEAFHOPPERS. EFFORTS TO MAP U.S. OCCURRENCE AND DISTRIBUTION OF OAK WILT HAVE BEEN COMPLICATED BY THE SIMILAR APPEARANCE OF CONSEQUENCES TO OAK OF THESE DIFFERENT BIOTIC AND ABIOTIC STRESSORS. IN THE URBAN LANDSCAPE AND NURSERY, INACCURATE DISEASE DIAGNOSIS CAN LEAD TO OVER-RELIANCE ON CHEMICAL PESTICIDES AND USE OF INEFFECTIVE TREATMENTS APPLIED TO CONTROL THE WRONG PROBLEM. THIS CONFUSION ALSO HAS RESULTED IN COMPLICATIONS FOR U.S. AGRICULTURE AND EXPORT COMMODITIES. HARVESTED LOGS INTENDED FOR INTERNATIONAL EXPORT ARE SUBJECT TO QUARANTINE WHEN ORIGINATING FROM LOCATIONS WITHIN THE U.S. WHERE OAK WILT IS DOCUMENTED. LOGS FROM THESE AREAS MUST BE PROVIDED PHYTOSANITARY TREATMENTS IN ORDER FOR EXPORT TO PROCEED. PENDING WITHDRAWAL OF THE PHYTOSANITARY FUMIGANT METHYL BROMIDE POTENTIALLY WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF ACCESS TO SOME EUROPEAN AND ASIAN MARKETS FOR AGROFORESTRY OAK LOGS.THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO THE HOST PLANT GENES THAT ARE ACTIVATED ACROSS TIME, AS A NATURAL METHOD OF HOST PLANT DEFENSE IN WHITE OAK AND RED OAK TREE SEEDLINGS, WHEN SUBJECTED TO INFECTION BY WITH THE OAK WILT PATHOGEN. EFFORTS WILL ALSO DOCUMENT THE GENES UP-REGULATED WITHIN A MOST VIRULENT AND A LEAST VIRULENT ISOLATE OF THE FUNGAL PATHOGEN WHEN ATTACKING TWO OAK HOST SPECIES, AS THE PATHOGEN SEEKS TO OVERCOME THE HOST PLANT DEFENSES. TAKEN TOGETHER, NEW SCIENCE ARISING FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL PROVIDE NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO HOST PLANT RESISTANCE THAT CAN INFORM FUTURE TREE BREEDING IN OAKS THAT YIELDS GREATER STRENGTH AND SUSTAINABILITY FOR THIS HIGHLY VALUED U.S. FOREST SPECIES AND AGRICULTURAL CROP COMMODITY. LASTLY, THIS RESEARCH COMPLIMENTS THE PARTICIPATING TEAM'S ONGOING EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A RAPID MOLECULAR TEST TO FACILITATE OAK WILT DIAGNOSIS AND DETECTION IN LANDSCAPE TREES, FOREST SPECIMENS, AND HARVESTED LOGS INTENDED FOR INTERNATIONAL EXPORT. IN COMBINATION, THESE APPROACHES ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE POWERFUL NEW TOOLS IN EFFORTS TO DELINEATE REGIONAL OCCURRENCE OF OAK WILT AND TO PREVENT ITS SPREAD INTO NEW, UNINFESTED LOCATIONS AROUND THE GLOBE.

THIS IS AN ARDP SINGLE-FUNCTION RESEARCH PROJECT FOCUSED ON PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS. WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF SATURATED STEAM AND ELECTRIC WEED CONTROL AS COMPONENTS OF A NON-CHEMICAL WEED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM. THESE NOVEL TECHNOLOGIES CAN FUNDAMENTALLY CHANGE WEED MANAGEMENT IN HAZELNUT TO MITIGATE HERBICIDE RESISTANCE. HERBICIDE RESISTANCE IS THE GREATEST WEED MANAGEMENT CHALLENGE IDENTIFIED IN MULTIPLE COMMODITIES. IN OREGON HAZELNUT ORCHARDS, THERE ARE CONFIRMED CASES OF RESISTANCE AND MULTIPLE-RESISTANCES TO ALL POST-EMERGENCE HERBICIDES, JEOPARDIZING HERBICIDE MIXTURES AND ROTATIONS AS A MANAGEMENT TOOL. THE USE OF NON-CHEMICAL WEED CONTROLS LIKE TILLAGE IS LIMITED IN HAZELNUT BECAUSE THE NUTS ARE HARVESTED FROM THE ORCHARD FLOOR, REQUIRING A LITTER-FREE AND FIRM SOIL SURFACE. OUR APPROACH INCLUDES FIELD RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION WITH GROWERS AND ON UNIVERSITY FARMS. NEITHER SATURATED STEAM NOR ELECTRIC WEED CONTROL DISTURBS THE SOIL, MAKING THEM COMPATIBLE WITH HAZELNUT. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS AND CROP SAFETY OF THE NOVEL TOOLS AS THEY COMPARE TO MOWING OR HERBICIDES. WE PROPOSE TO TEST TOOLS IN ORCHARD MIDDLES AND WITHIN TREE ROWS, AN AREA OF THE ORCHARD OFTEN MANAGED EXCLUSIVELY WITH HERBICIDES. EXPERIMENTS WILL DETERMINE SAFE RATES FOR STEAM AND ELECTRICITY APPLICATIONS WHILE OPTIMIZING WEED CONTROL. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP IDENTIFY EFFECTIVE NON-CHEMICAL WEED MANAGEMENT TOOLS COMPATIBLE WITH TREE NUT PRODUCTION. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A REDUCTION IN HERBICIDE RELIANCE, MITIGATION OF HERBICIDE RESISTANCE COSTS, AND REDUCED HUMAN EXPOSURE TO CHEMICALS. OUR FINDINGS WILL HAVE APPLICATIONS TO A WIDE RANGE OF OTHER WOODY PERENNIAL CROPS.

MASSACHUSETTS IS THE 3RD MOST DENSELY POPULATED STATE; MA FARM LAND IS VERY VALUABLE AND OFTEN SOUGHT AFTER FOR DEVELOPMENT. DESPITE THIS PRESSURE, FARMERS STEWARD OVER 523,500 ACRES, >10% OF THE MA LAND BASE. THERE ARE 7,755 FARMS (OF WHICH 2,651 ARE VEGETABLE, BERRY, AND FRUIT FARMS) IN THE STATE. THE TOTAL NUMBER OF FARMS HAS BEEN STEADY SINCE 2007, HOWEVER THE NUMBER OF VEGETABLE FARMS INCREASED BY MORE THAN 400 (28%) IN THE SAME TIME FRAME. AVERAGING 68 ACRES IN SIZE, 95% OF MA FARMS EASILY FIT THE USDA DEFINITION OF SMALL FARMS, BRINGING IN LESS THAN $64,000 ANNUALLY. EVEN WITH CONSTANT ECONOMIC AND BIOLOGICAL PRESSURES, MA FARMERS ARE COMMITTED TO BEING EFFICIENT BUSINESS OWNERS AND EFFECTIVE PEST MANAGERS, OPTIMIZING THE OUTPUT OF THEIR SMALL-SCALE SPECIALTY CROP FARMS TO MEET CONSUMER DEMANDS. MA FARMS GENERATE OVER $490 MILLION IN TOTAL SALES PER YEAR WITH 47% FROM SALES OF SPECIALTY CROPS SUCH AS APPLES, STRAWBERRIES, AND CUCURBITS. MA HAS ALMOST 300 FARMERS' MARKETSAND RANKS 1ST NATIONALLY BY PERCENTAGE OF FARMS WITH COMMUNITY SUPPORTED AGRICULTURE (CSA).THROUGH INCREASED ADOPTION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EFFECTIVE IPM STRATEGIES, THIS EIP PROJECT WILL SUPPORT NATIONAL INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) ROAD MAP GOALS OF ACHIEVING INCREASED PROFITABILITY WHILE REDUCING HUMAN HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS. OUR LEADERSHIP AND PARTNERSHIP ROLES WITH EXTENSION COLLEAGUES IN NEW ENGLAND AND INDUSTRY AND REGULATORY ORGANIZATIONS WILL CONTINUE TO FURTHER IPM IMPLEMENTATION FOR SPECIALTY CROP FARMS IN MA. RESPONDING TO STAKEHOLDER-IDENTIFIED NEEDS, WE WILL EXPAND OUR SKILL CAPACITY BY PARTICIPATING IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS TO IMPROVE TECHNICAL AND EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT FOR MA SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS.

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** KEY CHALLENGES FACED BY ORGANIC AND CONVENTIONAL PRODUCERS INCLUDE MANAGING MULTIPLE PEST COMPLEXES WHILE BEING HOSPITABLE TO BENEFICIAL ORGANISMS. THOUGH USING ORGANIC AND SOFT PESTICIDES SUCH AS PLANT-BASED INSECTICIDES AND TILLAGE CAN SUPPRESS INSECT AND WEED PESTS, THESE PRACTICES CAN HAVE NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ON BENEFICIAL ORGANISMS ABOVE AND BELOW THE SOIL. GENERALLY, THESE TWO PEST COMPLEXES ARE STUDIED SEPARATELY. HOWEVER, THERE EXISTS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS THESE PEST ISSUES CONCOMITANTLY, AND CONSEQUENTLY DEVELOP PEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES THAT ADDRESS CROP VULNERABILITY TO INSECTS, WEEDS AND NEMATODES WITHOUT COMPROMISING AGROECOSYSTEM HEALTH. THUS, THE GOAL OF OUR MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM IS TO DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE HUSBANDRY PRACTICES THAT WILL HELP PRODUCERS MITIGATE MULTIPLE PEST COMPLEXES WITHOUT IMPAIRING BENEFICIAL ORGANISMS. THREE ECOFRIENDLY PRACTICES (BIOSOLARIZATION, COVER CROPPING, AND STRIP-TILLAGE) WILL BE DEPLOYED AND INVESTIGATED JOINTLY. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE, LOW COST AND LOW INPUT PRACTICES TO IMPROVE SOIL HEALTH, PEST SUPPRESSION AND CROP PRODUCTIVITY ON CONVENTIONAL AND ORGANIC FARMS. TO THIS END, FIELD TRIALS AND/OR EXTENSION ACTIVITIES WILL OCCUR AT UNIVERSITY AND FARMERS' FIELD SITES. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO DEMONSTRATE THE SYNERGISTIC BENEFITS OF BIOSOLARIZATION, COVER CROPPING AND STRIP TILLAGE FOR: (1) REDUCING CROP PESTS; (2) ENHANCING YIELDS AND BENEFICIAL ORGANISMS BELOW AND ABOVE THE SOIL; AND (3) DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE GAINED FROM OBJECTIVES 1 AND 2 TO STAKEHOLDERS.

THIS IS AN APPLIED RESEARCH (ARDP SINGLE-FUNCTION) MULTI-STATE PROJECT THAT CONTRIBUTES TO CPPM FOCUS AREA 1 - PLANT PROTECTION TACTICS AND TOOLS. STAKEHOLDERS FROM ACROSS MIDWEST SOUTH AND CENTRAL GREAT PLAINS OF THE U.S. HAVE IDENTIFIED PIGWEEDS (PALMER AMARANTH AND WATERHEMP) AS ONE OF THE MOST PROBLEMATIC AND ECONOMICALLY DAMAGING WEED SPECIES. BOTH PIGWEEDS CURRENTLY POSE A SERIOUS THREAT TO SUSTAINABLE CROP PRODUCTION DUE TO A LIMITED EFFECTIVE HERBICIDE OPTIONS. IMPLEMENTATION AND ADOPTION OF THESE ECOLOGICALLY-BASED IWM STRATEGIES WILL REDUCE POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND APPLICATOR EXPOSURE PROBLEMS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED PESTICIDE USE. positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THIS IS A MULTI-STATE/MULTI-REGIONAL, APPLIED (SINGLE-FUNCTION) RESEARCH-LED PROPOSAL ADDRESSING THE PLANT PROTECTION TACTICS AND TOOLS CPPM FOCUS AREA. THERE IS A GROWING DEMAND FOR HEMP-DERIVED PRODUCTS IN THE UNITED STATES (US). RECENT ESTIMATES SUGGEST THAT HEMP PRODUCT SALES IN THE US ARE VALUED AT $700 MILLION. BECAUSE OF THE CROP'S PREVIOUS DESIGNATION AS A SCHEDULE 1 SUBSTANCE AND HISTORY OF CRIMINALIZATION, THERE IS LIMITED UNIVERSITY-PRODUCED INFORMATION DESCRIBING BEST PRODUCTION PRACTICES, WHICH INCLUDES INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT (IWM). OUR GOALS ARE 1) DESCRIBE THE COMPETITIVENESS OF GRAIN, FIBER, AND FLORAL HEMP WITH WEEDS, 2) EVALUATE THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN THIS EMERGING CROP, AND 3) DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE EXTENSION MATERIALS. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE STUDIES, WHICH WILL BE CONDUCTED IN NY, VA, SC, IL, AND ND, TO DEFINE THE CRITICAL TIMING OF WEED MANAGEMENT OPERATIONS AGAINST COMMON AND TROUBLESOME WEEDS AND DESCRIBE THE IMPACTS OF CHEMICAL, PHYSICAL, AND CULTURAL PRACTICES ON THE SUPPRESSION OF UNWANTED VEGETATION. RESULTS FROM ROBUST AND REPLICATED STUDIES WILL BE SHARED WITH LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL STAKEHOLDERS TO REDUCE THE KNOWLEDGE GAP THAT CURRENTLY EXISTS FOR THIS ANCIENT, YET EMERGING, COMMODITY. ULTIMATE OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK INCLUDE INCREASED GROWER KNOWLEDGE REGARDING IWM IN HEMP, ALTERED PRODUCTION PRACTICES, AND ENHANCED AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTIVITY. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS THE CPPM GOAL OF SUSTAINABLE FOOD SECURITY THROUGH THE IMPROVEMENT OF IWM PRACTICES THAT INCREASES IPM ADOPTION AND REDUCES ENVIRONMENTAL AND HUMAN HEALTH RISKS WHILE SUPPORTING FARMER PROFITABILITY.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE EVOLUTION AND SPREAD OF GLYPHOSATE AND MULTIPLE HERBICIDE-RESISTANT WEEDS HAS LED TO SIGNIFICANT INCREASES IN HERBICIDE USE AND FARM-LEVEL WEED CONTROL COSTS WITHIN NO-TILL FIELD CROP PRODUCTIONS SYSTEMS ACROSS U.S. REGIONS.DEVELOPMENT AND COMMUNICATION OF PROACTIVE, INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT (IWM) STRATEGIES THAT EMPLOY NON-CHEMICAL TACTICS TO REDUCE THE LIKELIHOOD OF HERBICIDE RESISTANCE EVOLUTION IS URGENTLY NEEDED. COVER CROPPING IS UNIQUE AMONG POTENTIAL IWM TACTICS IN THAT CURRENT INTEREST AND ADOPTION IS PRIMARILY DRIVEN BY LONG-TERM SUSTAINABLE AGROECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT GOALS. UNDERSTANDING OF INTERACTIONS BETWEEN HIGH-RESIDUE COVER CROPS AND USE OF SOIL-APPLIED RESIDUAL HERBICIDES IS A SIGNIFICANT KNOWLEDGE GAP THAT PREVENTS IMPROVED EFFICACY OF INTEGRATED TACTICS. OUR GOAL IS TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW HIGH-RESIDUE COVER CROP MANAGEMENT TACTICS (TERMINATION TIMING, SPECIES SELECTION, RESIDUE MANAGEMENT) INFLUENCE THE FATE AND EFFICACY OF SOIL-APPLIED RESIDUAL HERBICIDES. FIELD EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO (1) QUANTIFY THE INTERACTIVE EFFECTS OF COVER CROP RESIDUE AND RESIDUAL HERBICIDE PROPERTIES ON HERBICIDE FATE PROCESSES, INCLUDING INTERCEPTION, RETENTION, AND SOIL BIOAVAILABILITY, AND (2) EVALUATE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN HIGH-RESIDUE COVER CROP AND RESIDUAL HERBICIDE MANAGEMENT TACTICS ON POPULATION DYNAMICS OF MULTIPLE HERBICIDE RESISTANT WEEDS. ANTICIPATED IMPACTS OF OUR INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECT INCLUDE IMPROVED PRODUCER KNOWLEDGE OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (BMPS), CONCEPTUAL APPROACHES, AND LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT GOALS FOR EMPLOYING PROACTIVE IWM TO MANAGE AND PREVENT HERBICIDE RESISTANCE.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** MOST OF THE CORN AND COTTON GROWN IN THE US, EXPRESSES BT TOXINS DESIGNED TO KILL MAJOR INSECT PESTS. THE US CATEGORIZES BT TOXINS AS PUBLIC GOODS AT RISK OF BEING LOST DUE TO RESISTANCE. CORN GROWERS ARE REQUIRED TO PLANT 20% OF THEIR TOTAL CORN ACRES TO NON-BT (REFUGE) CORN TO DELAY THE EVOLUTION OF BT RESISTANCE. HOWEVER, VERY FEW GROWERS PLANT NON-BT CORN, PRIMARILY BECAUSE INSECTICIDE SUSCEPTIBILITY IS A COMMON POOL RESOURCE. PRIOR RESEARCH FROM OUR GROUP HAS SHOWN THAT MAJOR SEED COMPANIES HAVE HIGH-YIELDING NON-BT HYBRIDS AVAILABLE. OUR PROPOSAL WILL DEMONSTRATE THE YIELD POTENTIAL OF THESE NON-BT HYBRIDS PAIRED WITH CLOSELY RELATED BT HYBRIDS. WE WILL DO THIS ON 45 FARMS AND IN 13 OFFICIAL VARIETY TESTING FOR EACH OF TWO YEARS ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA AND VIRGINIA. WE WILL ALSO TRAIN COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AGENTS ON GENERAL CORN AGRONOMY AND HOW TO IDENTIFY INSECT DAMAGE SO THAT THEY CAN COLLECT DATA. THIS DATA WILL FEED INTO A DAMAGE ABATEMENT MODEL TO ESTIMATE THE SHORT RUN-IMPACTS OF NON-BT HYBRIDS, AS WELL AS A LONG-RUN ECONOMIC ANALYSIS TO ACCOUNT FOR THE DIFFERENCE IN THE EVOLUTION OF RESISTANCE WHEN PLANTING NON-BT HYBRIDS. FINALLY, THIS INFORMATION WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH PUBLICATION ON THE NORTH CAROLINA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION CORN PORTAL, PRESENTATIONS IN COUNTY WINTER MEETINGS, AND THROUGH INCORPORATION INTO THE VARIETY SELECTION TOOL DATABASE. GROWERS USE THIS TOOL TO SELECT HYBRIDS APPROPRIATE FOR THEIR FARM BASED ON DATA GATHERED FROM NC OFFICIAL VARIETY TRIALS PLANTED IN MULTIPLE LOCATIONS ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE CURRENT PROPOSAL IS AN ARDP APPLIED RESEARCH (SINGLE-FUNCTION) PROJECT. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES THE PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS CPPM FOCUS AREA, WITH EMPHASIS ON CERCOSPORA LEAF BLIGHT (CLB) OF SOYBEAN. SOYBEAN GROWERS IN THE MID-SOUTH HAVE STRUGGLED WITH THE MANAGEMENT OF CLB FOR NEARLY TWO DECADES; CLB EPIDEMIOLOGY WAS UNCLEAR, RESISTANCE IN COMMERCIAL SOYBEAN CULTIVARS WAS LIMITED, FEW FUNGICIDES WERE EFFECTIVE AGAINST THE PATHOGEN, AND RESISTANCE TO COMMONLY USED FUNGICIDES WAS WIDESPREAD. THUS, OVER THE PAST FIVE YEARS, LOSSES DUE TO CLB ACROSS AR, LA, AND MS IS ESTIMATED TO HAVE BEEN >$250 MILLION. RECENTLY, RESEARCH IN THE MID-SOUTH HAS PROVIDED NEW INSIGHTS INTO SOURCES OF CLB INOCULUM, DOCUMENTED SOME RESISTANCE IN COMMERCIAL CULTIVARS, AND IDENTIFIED NEW FUNGICIDES EFFECTIVE AGAINST THE DISEASE. HOWEVER, KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN IN THE INTRICACIES OF CLB EPIDEMIOLOGY, MANAGEMENT OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANCE PROBLEMS, AND INTEGRATION OF ALL AVAILABLE TOOLS TO IMPROVE CLB MANAGEMENT. THIS PROJECT IS A COLLABORATIVE MULTI-STATE EFFORT THAT AIMS TO ADVANCE RESEARCH INSIGHTS GENERATED FROM STAKEHOLDER SUPPORTED PROJECTS AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND AND TARGET CLB MANAGEMENT. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT ARE TO 1) DETERMINE THE IMPORTANCE OF AIR-BORNE CONIDIA IN THE DISEASE CYCLE AND IDENTIFY ENVIRONMENTAL PREDICTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE DEVELOPMENT, 2) DEVELOP TOOLS TO RAPIDLY MONITOR RESISTANCE TO COMMONLY USED FUNGICIDE CHEMISTRIES, AND 3) INTEGRATE IMPROVED FUNGICIDE APPLICATION TIMING AND HOST RESISTANCE IN CLB DISEASE MANAGEMENT. TOGETHER, THE PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE, LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT SOLUTIONS FOR CLB, CRUCIAL TO PROTECT THE $41 BILLION US SOYBEAN CROP.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE MANAGEMENT OF SPOTTED-WING DROSOPHILA (SWD), DROSOPHILA SUZUKII (MATSUMURA), A KEY PEST OF SOFT-SKINNED FRUIT CROPS IN THE USA. SINCE 2008, IT HAS CONTINUED TO IMPACT FRUIT CROPS SEVERELY, AND IMPLEMENTING COST-EFFECTIVE, SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS REMAINS AN URGENT NATIONAL PRIORITY. THERE IS ZERO TOLERANCE FOR THE INFESTATION IN FRESH FRUIT, SO MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS RELY ON BROAD-SPECTRUM INSECTICIDES, RESULTING IN SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC AND NON-TARGET EFFECTS. THE INTENSIVE MANAGEMENT FOR THIS PEST INCLUDES SECONDARY PEST OUTBREAKS THAT OCCUR WHEN INSECTICIDES DISRUPT OTHER PESTS' BIOLOGICAL CONTROL. THEREFORE, NEW NON-INSECTICIDE MANAGEMENT OPTIONS ARE NEEDED. THE MOST PROMISING BIOLOGICAL CONTROL OPTION IS INTRODUCING A PARASITOID FROM THE NATIVE RANGE OF SWD IN ASIA. RECENT EXPLORATIONS AND SUBSEQUENT RESEARCH HAVE IDENTIFIED GANASPIS BRASILIENSIS, A LARVAL PARASITOID, AS ONE OF THE MOST EFFICIENT AND HOST-SPECIFIC SWD PARASITOIDS. IN ADDITIONTO BIOLOGICAL CONTROL OPTIONS, PROMISING NEW BEHAVIORAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, INCLUDING REPELLENTS, ATTRACT AND KILL AND BAIT METHODS ARE IN DEVELOPMENT. THESE STRATEGIES ARE REDUCED RISK COMPARED TO THE CURRENT INSECTICIDE USAGE. CURRENTLY, LITTLE IS KNOWN IF G. BRASILIENSIS WILL SUCCESSFULLY ESTABLISH, OVERWINTER, OR BE COMPATIBLE WITH NEW BEHAVIORAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES. WE PROPOSE TO FURTHER OUR KNOWLEDGE ON THE ESTABLISHMENT, OVERWINTERING SUCCESS, AND CONSERVATION OF G. BRASILIENSIS THROUGH INTEGRATION WITH BEHAVIORAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** MANY FRESH MARKET VEGETABLES, PARTICULARLY TOMATOES, ARE INCREASINGLY PRODUCED IN HIGH TUNNELS (HTS) TO EXTEND THE GROWING SEASON AND CAPTURE LUCRATIVE MARKETS. INCREASED DEMAND FOR LOCAL PRODUCE HAS ALSO LED TO A SHIFT IN HIGH VALUE VEGETABLE PRODUCTION FROM OPENFIELDS TO PROTECTED CULTURE. IN ADDITION, CLIMATE DISRUPTIONS HAVE MADE PROTECTED CULTURE DESIRABLE AS A MEANS OF ESCAPING FOLIAR BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL DISEASES INTENSIFIED BY RAIN. IT IS NOT UNCOMMON FOR TOMATOES TO BE PRODUCED IN THE SAME HT EACH YEAR FOR 5 YEARS OR MORE. MANY GROWERS HAVE INTENSIFIED PRODUCTION AND ADDED FEATURES, SUCH AS HEATING AND COOLING SYSTEMS, THAT MAKE THE TUNNELS DIFFICULT AND EXPENSIVE TO MOVE. THE RESULTING LIMITED ROTATIONS HAVE CAUSED SOILBORNE PATHOGEN POPULATIONS TO BUILD UP, AND YIELD AND FRUIT QUALITY ARE GREATLY REDUCED. SOILBORNE DISEASES THREATEN THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF TOMATO PRODUCTION IN HTS IF LEFT UNCHECKED. KEY SOILBORNE DISEASES INCLUDE VERTICILLIUM WILT (VERTICILLIUM DAHLIAE), BLACK DOT ROOT ROT (COLLETOTRICHUM COCCODES), CORKY ROOT ROT (PYRENOCHAETA LYCOPERSICI), AND ROOT-KNOT (MELOIDOGYNE SPP.). THE SOILBORNE DISEASE COMPLEX OF TOMATO WAS FIRST IDENTIFIED IN OH IN 2015 AND IS NOW WIDESPREAD WITH P. LYCOPERSICIIN 46%, C. COCCODES IN 90%, V. DAHLIAE IN 48% AND MELOIDOGYNE SPP. IN 45% OF HTS SURVEYED. RECENT SURVEYS IN PA HAVE ALSO IDENTIFIED ACTIONABLE LEVELS OF MELOIDOGYNE SPP. IN 42% OF HTS AMONG OTHER PATHOGENS, SUCH AS SCLEROTINIA SCLEROTIORUM. DISEASE DIAGNOSTIC CLINICS IN VA HAVE ROUTINELY DETECTED ABOVE THRESHOLD LEVELS OF ROOT-KNOT NEMATODES AND EXCESSIVE DAMAGE CAUSED BY SOUTHERN BLIGHT (SCLEROTIUM ROLFSII). HIGH TUNNEL TOMATOES ARE THE MAINSTAY OF LOCAL VEGETABLE PRODUCTION AND YIELD AND QUALITY LOSSES DUE TO SOILBORNE DISEASES NOT ONLY LIMIT FARM SUSTAINABILITY BUT ALSO AFFECT CONSUMER PRICES AND PRODUCE AVAILABILITY.SOILBORNE DISEASE MANAGEMENT RELIES ON GROWERS' KNOWLEDGE OF DISEASES PRESENT ON THEIR FARMS AND AVAILABLE MANAGEMENT OPTIONS. SOILBORNE DISEASE DIAGNOSIS IS HINDERED BY THE HIDDEN NATURE OF ROOTS, THE HETEROGENEOUS DISTRIBUTION OF SOILBORNE PATHOGENS, THE COMPLEXITY OF THE SOIL MATRIX AND THE LACK OF DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES. ACCESS TO AN AFFORDABLE, STANDARDIZED SOILBORNE DISEASE TESTING SERVICE FOR THE MOST PREVALENT SOILBORNE PATHOGENS OF TOMATO WOULD PROVIDE GROWERS WITH ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE OF THEIR SOIL'S STATUS REGARDING PATHOGENS. A SOILBORNE DISEASE TESTING PROTOCOL RECENTLY DEVELOPED AND DEPLOYED IN OH WILL BE USED TO TEST SOIL SAMPLES COLLECTED IN HTS IN OH, PA AND VA. GROWERS WILL RECEIVE CUSTOMIZED DIAGNOSTIC REPORTS WITH MANAGEMENT RECOOMENDATIONS. MANAGEMENT OF SOILBORNE DISEASES HISTORICALLY RELIED ON ENVIRONMENTALLY DAMAGING, ENERGY INTENSIVE METHODS, INCLUDING FUMIGATION AND STEAM STERILIZATION. ANAEROBIC SOIL DISINFESTATION (ASD) IS A BIOLOGICAL PROCESS THAT REDUCESS OR ELIMINATE POPULATIONS OF SOILBORNE PLANT PATHOGENS, WEEDS AND SOILBORNE INSECT PESTS. WE WILL INCRREASE AWARENESS OF ASD,AMONG HT TOMATO GROWERS BY CONDUCTING ON-FARM MOTHER AND BABY TRIALS IN EACH STATE. FARMERS (N=27) WILL TEST ASD IN THEIR HTS (BABY TRIALS) AND PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON EFFICACY AND POTENTIAL ADOPTION. FULLY REPLICATED MOTHER TRIALS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO DEMONSTRATE DIFFERENT ASD TREATMENTS. SINCE ASD RELIES ON SOIL AMENDMENT WITH A SOURCE OF CARBON, USUALLY AGRICULTURAL BYPRODUCTS LIKE WHEAT MIDDS OR SPENT DISTILLER'S GRAINS, RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO OPTIMIZE NUTRITION FOR TOMATOES. STUDIES WILL BE CONDUCTED TO UNDERSTAND NUTRIENT DYNAMICS AND AVAILABILITY AFTER ASD WITH DIFFERENT CARBON SOURCES, RESULTING IN NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR GROWERS. FINALLY, RESULTS OF THE PROJECT WILL BE COMMUNICATED TO STAKEHOLDERS USING FACTSHEETS, SHORT VIDEOS, WEBINARS, BLOGS, AND ONLINE AND IN-PERSON PRESENTATIONS TO GROWER GROUPS. PROJECT PROGRESS WILL BE MONITORED AND POTENTIAL ADOPTION OF ASD PREDICTED USING OUTCOOME MAPPING. ULTIMATELY, THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE TOMATO PRODUCTION IN HTS, PROMOTE WIDESPREAD ADOPTION OF ASD, AND ENSURE THE AVAILABILITY OF HIGH QUALITY LOCAL TOMATOES TO CONSUMERS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE MULTIPLE HERBICIDE-RESISTANT (MHR) WEED EPIDEMIC IS THREATENING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF KEY AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES BY RENDERING VALUABLE HERBICIDES INEFFECTIVE. MHR IS CAUSING REDUCED CROP YIELDS, INCREASED WEED MANAGEMENT COSTS, AND INCREASED RELIANCE ON HERBICIDES WITH GREATER ENVIRONMENTAL PERSISTENCE, WHICH THREATENS A REVERSION TO TILLAGE, NEGATING DECADES OF SOIL HEALTH AND CONSERVATION GAINS. SEED IMPACT MILLS PROCESS AND KILL THE VAST MAJORITY OF WEED SEEDS AS THEY EXIT THE COMBINE DURING CROP HARVEST. THIS NEW TECHNOLOGY IS BEING RAPIDLY AND WIDELY ADOPTED IN AUSTRALIA, WHERE IT IS PROVIDING AN EFFECTIVE INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT TOOL FOR MHR. HOWEVER, WE ARE YET TO FULLY UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THIS SYSTEM UNDER US PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. OUR MULTI-STATE, MULTI-REGION TEAM HAS 12 SEED IMPACT MILLS ON-FARM ACROSS OUR NETWORK, A POSITION ENJOYED BY NO OTHER GROUP. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THIS FARMER COOPERATIVE ON-FARM RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECT ARE TO COMPREHENSIVELY EVALUATE SEED IMPACT MILL EFFICACY FOR ECONOMIC DECISION DRIVER WEEDS IN SOYBEAN AND WHEAT AND COMMUNICATE THESE RESULTS TO GROWERS THROUGH OUR GROW (GETTING RID OF WEEDS) WEBSITE, SOCIAL MEDIA, DEVELOPING EXTENSION BULLETINS, INTERACTIVE WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS, AND PEER-TO-PEER LEARNING THROUGH ON-FARM PROGRAMS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL DETERMINE OPERATING COSTS OF SEED IMPACT MILLS AND CREATE A COST CALCULATOR DECISION SUPPORT TOOL FOR USING THIS TECHNOLOGY. WE ANTICIPATE THAT THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE ADOPTION OF SEED IMPACT MILL TECHNOLOGY IN US SOYBEAN AND WHEAT PRODUCTION, REDUCING THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPACT, AND SPREAD OF MHR WEEDS, AND INCREASING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF CROP PRODUCTION.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** SCB IS ROUTINELY RANKED AS THE TOP INSECT PEST AMONG VEGETABLE GROWERS NATIONWIDE, NOT JUST IN CUCURBITS BUT ACROSS ALL CROP TYPES. IN A SURVEY OF >1,000 DIVERSIFIED ORGANIC AND TRANSITIONING VEGETABLE GROWERS FROM ACROSS 16 EASTERN U.S. STATES, CUCUMBER BEETLE WAS THE MOST FREQUENTLY NAMED PEST WHEN FARMERS WERE ASKED TO IDENTIFY WHICH INSECTS ARE 'USUALLY PRESENT' AND 'DIFFICULT TO CONTROL' (I. KAPLAN, UNPUBLISHED DATA). WE ALSO CONDUCTED A RECENT (2019) SURVEY OF 106 CONVENTIONAL CUCURBIT PRODUCERS IN THE PD'S STUDY REGION (INDIANA, ILLINOIS, MICHIGAN, OHIO), RESULTING IN SIMILAR RESPONSES. CUCUMBER BEETLES WERE IDENTIFIED BY 77% OF THE RESPONDENTS AS PRESENT IN THEIR FIELDS AND WAS THE TOP INSECT LISTED WHEN ASKED TO WRITE IN WHICH INSECT DID YOU HAVE THE MOST PROBLEMS MANAGING IN YOUR CUCURBIT FIELDS IN 2018?.THE OUTCOME FROM THESE DIRECT MAIL SURVEYS CORRESPONDS WELL WITH NUMEROUS STATE- AND CROP-SPECIFIC REPORTS OF STAKEHOLDER-IDENTIFIED IPM NEEDS FROM THE NATIONAL INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT DATABASE (HTTPS://IPMDATA.IPMCENTERS.ORG/). THE SCB IS MENTIONED AS A PRIMARY PEST OF CONCERN IN VIRTUALLY ALL EASTERN U.S. CUCURBIT CROP PROFILES, INFESTING 78-100% OF ACREAGE. EXAMPLES OF SPECIFIC REPORTS INCLUDE:PUMPKINS IN VIRGINIA: BOTH THE SPOTTED AND STRIPED CUCUMBER BEETLES (ADULTS AND LARVAE) MAY SEVERELY REDUCE PUMPKIN PRODUCTIVITY. THESE PESTS ARE THE #1 CONCERN OF GROWERS IN VIRGINIA.WATERMELONS IN MISSOURI: THE PRIMARY INSECT/MITE PESTS AFFECTING WATERMELON PRODUCTION ANNUALLY IN MISSOURI ARE THE CUCUMBER BEETLE AND SPIDER MITES. THE CUCUMBER BEETLE IS THE NUMBER ONE INSECT PEST.SQUASH IN DELAWARE: STRIPED CUCUMBER BEETLES, ACALYMMA VITTATA (FABRICIUS), AND SPOTTED CUCUMBER BEETLES, DIABROTICA UNDECIMPUNETATA HOWARDI (BARBER), ARE THE MOST DESTRUCTIVE INSECT PESTS OF CUCUMBERS, SQUASH AND RELATED CROPS IN THE MID-ATLANTIC AREA.PUMPKINS IN PENNSYLVANIA: CUCUMBER BEETLES ARE A GROUP THAT ARE THE MOST SIGNIFICANT INSECT PEST OF MOST CUCURBITS.WATERMELON IN LOUISIANA: THE MAJOR INSECT PROBLEM ON WATERMELONS IS CUCUMBER BEETLES.MELONS IN CALIFORNIA: INSECTICIDES WERE USED ON 76% OF ALL CANTALOUPES GROWN IN CALIFORNIA...THE PRIMARY PESTS TO ALL MELON TYPES TARGETED BY THESE FOLIAR TREATMENTS INCLUDE...CUCUMBER BEETLES.LAST, OUR LOCAL OBSERVATIONS MATCH CONVERSATIONS WITH CUCURBIT (MOSTLY MELON) GROWERS AND ON-FARM PEST SAMPLING CONDUCTED BY THE PD AT 20 WATERMELON FARMS IN INDIANA BETWEEN 2017 AND 2018 (RESULTS REPORTED IN TERNEST ET AL. 2020). RECENTLY (APRIL 2020) WE ALSO PUBLISHED A SERIES OF VIDEOS, FEATURING INTERVIEWS WITH SOME OF THE LARGER MELON PRODUCERS IN THE MIDWEST, WHO DISCUSSED THEIR USE OF INSECTICIDES FOR SCB MANAGEMENT (HTTPS://YOUTU.BE/GRQONJ5EX0M) AND THEIR RELIANCE ON HONEY BEES OR WILD POLLINATORS (HTTPS://YOUTU.BE/CTZQ1PYGMFA). MOST MELON PRODUCTION IN THE WEST OCCURS IN CALIFORNIA, WHERE CUCUMBER BEETLES ARE PRIMARILY AN ISSUE IN THE NORTHERN CENTRAL VALLEY. HERE, THEY ARE A STAKEHOLDER-DEFINED PEST,ISSUE (CA PMSP 2016) AND ARE TYPICALLY DESCRIBED AS THE PRIMARY INSECT OF CONCERN BY PEST CONTROL ADVISORS AND GROWERS.WHILE THERE ARE CLEARLY REGIONAL DIFFERENCES IN PEST COMPLEXES AND SITE-SPECIFIC PEST HISTORIES OR ISSUES, THE ABOVE COMBINATION OF GROWER SURVEYS, IPM REPORTS, ON-FARM OBSERVATIONS, AND FARMER INTERVIEWS COLLECTIVELY IDENTIFY THE CUCUMBER BEETLE COMPLEX AS THE SINGLE GREATEST INSECT THREAT TO CUCURBIT PRODUCTION AND SUSTAINABILITY.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** SINCE THE 2013 INVASION OF THE SUGARCANE APHID (SCA) ON SORGHUM IN THE UNITED STATES, IPM SCIENTISTS AND PRACTITIONERS HAVE WORKED TOGETHER TO DEVELOP IPM PROGRAMS IN A DIVERSE SET OF GROWING REGIONS. IN THE SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS, WHERE NEARLY 80% OF GRAIN SORGHUM IS GROWN, IPM PROGRAMS ARE CURRENTLY BASED ON DEPLOYMENT OF VARIETAL RESISTANCE, RELIABLE APHID ECONOMIC THRESHOLDS, EFFICIENT SAMPLING PLANS, AND CONSERVATION OF NATURAL ENEMIES THROUGH JUDICIOUS USE OF INSECTICIDES. A FINAL MISSING COMPONENT IS THE INTEGRATION OF NATURAL ENEMY THRESHOLDS INTO SCA MANAGEMENT PLANS. OUR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION TEAM WILL VALIDATE AND REFINE PRELIMINARY NE THRESHOLDS FOR SCA IN SORGHUM AT THE WHOLE-FIELD LEVEL IN A DIVERSE SET OF GROWING CONDITIONS THROUGHOUT THE REGION, INTEGRATE APHID AND NE SAMPLING PLANS, AND DELIVER AND EVALUATE THE ADOPTION OF THESE PLANS IN THE US SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS. WE ANTICIPATE THAT A LARGE PERCENTAGE OF PRODUCERS AND IPM PRACTITIONERS WILL UTILIZE NE+SCA THRESHOLDS IN GRAIN SORGHUM. WIDESPREAD USE OF THESE NEWLY AVAILABLE COMBINED THRESHOLDS AGAINST THE INVASIVE SCA WILL ENHANCE SUSTAINABLE SORGHUM PRODUCTION.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** INTENSIFICATIONS OF AGRICULTURE, GLOBAL TRADE, AND CLIMATE CHANGE ARE DRIVING UNPRECEDENTED ECOLOGICAL CHANGES, INCLUDING THE EMERGENCE OF PLANT-INFECTING VIRUSES IN NEW LOCATIONS. THESE PATHOGENS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR BILLIONS OF DOLLARS IN LOST REVENUE ANNUALLY AND POSE THREATS TO NATIVE VEGETATION DUE TO SPILLOVER FROM AGRICULTURE. NUTRIENT-RICH SPECIALTY CROPS, SUCH AS MUSKMELONS (CANTALOUPE AND HONEYDEW), ARE PARTICULARLY PRONE TO LOSSES FROM PLANT VIRUSES BECAUSE VIRUS INFECTION IMPACTS BOTH THE AMOUNT OF FRUITS PRODUCED AS WELL AS THEIR APPEARANCE, TASTE, AND MARKETABILITY. OVER THE LAST 30 YEARS, MUSKMELON GROWERS IN THE US HAVE ENDURED THE REPEATED INTRODUCTION AND ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW INSECT VECTORS (TRANSMITTERS OF PLANT VIRUSES) AND NEW VIRAL PATHOGENS. THIS HAS RESULTED IN INTENSIVE USE OF INSECTICIDES TO CONTROL INSECT VECTORS, LEADING TO NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS, HIGH COSTS, AND ONLY MARGINAL VIRUS CONTROL. THUS, IMPORTANT ECONOMIC, ECOLOGICAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL MOTIVATIONS EXIST TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) APPROACHES TO MANAGE THE IMPACTS OF BOTH VIRUSES AND VECTORS. OUR PROPOSED ACTIVITIES WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THIS STAKEHOLDER-IDENTIFIED NEED THROUGH TESTING AND VALIDATION OF RESISTANCE-BASED IPM TOOLS THAT WILL PROVIDE FLEXIBLE, SUSTAINABLE VIRUS CONTROL OPTIONS COMPATIBLE WITH REDUCED RISK INSECTICIDE PROGRAMS. WE WILL LEVERAGE SEVERAL YEARS OF BREEDING RESEARCH, FUNDED BY STAKEHOLDERS, TO CREATE NEW MUSKMELON CULTIVARS WITH VIRUS AND VECTOR RESISTANCE. THIS WILL PROVIDE SOLUTIONS FOR THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE VIRUS AND VECTOR THREATS. TO ADDRESS EMERGING VIRUS CONCERNS AND ESTABLISHED PATHOGEN COMPLEXES (GROUPS OF CO-OCCURRING VIRUSES), WE WILL PERFORM GREENHOUSE TRIALS TO EVALUATE RESISTANT MELON PERFORMANCE AGAINST THESE VIRUSES IN COMBINATION WITH PLANT IMMUNITY PRIMING (PLANT VACCINATION) AS A TOOL FOR ENHANCING RESISTANCE AND BOLSTERING INNATE IMMUNITY. FINALLY, TO EVALUATE RESISTANCE AND PRIMING EFFICACY, ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY, AND POTENTIAL PESTICIDE REDUCTIONS, WE WILL CARRY OUT FIELD TRIALS AND PARTNER WITH AN AGRICULTURAL ECONOMIST TO PRODUCE A COST-RETURN ANALYSIS AND COMMUNICATE RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS. GIVEN THE SUCCESS OF OUR PRIOR WORK, WE ANTICIPATE THAT OUTPUTS OF THIS PROJECT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE EXISTING PEST MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS AND SERVE AS A MODEL FOR SIMILAR VIRUS MANAGEMENT APPROACHES IN OTHER VEGETABLE CROPS AFFECTED BY COMPLICATED VIRUS-VECTOR PROBLEMS.

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** APPLES ARE ONE OF THE TOPMOST CONSUMED FRUIT IN THE UNITED STATES, SECOND IN POPULARITY ONLY TO BANANAS. THEY HAVE AN ANNUAL FARM-GATE VALUE OF NEARLY US$4 BILLION, WITH DOWNSTREAM REVENUES EXCEEDING US$15 BILLION. APPLES ARE AVAILABLE AND ENJOYED YEAR-ROUND BECAUSE THEY CAN BE HELD IN COLD STORAGE UNDER CONTROLLED ATMOSPHERE CONDITIONS, WHICH SUSPENDS THE RIPENING PROCESS SUCH THAT AN APPLE MAINTAINS ITS CRISPNESS AND TASTE 9-11 MONTHS AFTER THEY WERE HARVESTED. POSTHARVEST ROT DURING STORAGE CAUSED BY FUNGAL PATHOGENS IS A PERSISTENT THREAT TO THE GLOBAL US APPLE INDUSTRY. THIS NOT ONLY REDUCES THEIR QUALITY, INCREASES FOOD LOSS, BUT ALSO CAN LEAD TO MYCOTOXIN CONTAMINATION OF PROCESSED FRUIT PRODUCTS. ANNUAL LOSSES DUE TO POSTHARVEST ROTS RANGE BETWEEN 1%-15% IN THE UNITED STATES, ALONE. CURRENT ESTIMATES OF THE ECONOMIC LOSSES DUE TO POSTHARVEST APPLE ROTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE; HOWEVER, ESTIMATING 15% LOSS OF THE 4.5-5 MILLION TONNES OF APPLES PRODUCED ANNUALLY IN THE UNITED STATES, AND AN AVERAGE PRICE OF US$1.5 PER POUND, UP TO US$2.5 BILLION ARE LOST EACH YEAR DUE TO POSTHARVEST ROTS. APPROXIMATELY A DOZEN DISEASES CAN AFFECT APPLES DURING STORAGE. THE MOST FREQUENT POSTHARVEST ROTS OF APPLES ARE BLUE MOLD, CAUSED BY PENICILLIUM EXPANSUM AND OTHER PENICILLIUM SPP., AND GRAY MOLD, CAUSED BY BOTRYTIS CINEREA. THE FUNGI CAUSING BLUE MOLD ARE OF MOST CONCERN SINCE SEVERAL OF THE SPECIES PRODUCE THE MYCOTOXIN PATULIN. UNFORTUNATELY, NO APPLE VARIETIES EXIST THAT ARE RESISTANT TO THESE DISEASES AND MANAGEMENT OPTIONS OF POSTHARVEST APPLE ROT ARE LIMITED. GROWERS RELY ON CONTINUED USE OF SYNTHETIC FUNGICIDES, WHICH THERE ARE FEW AND HAVE CAUSED THE EMERGENCE OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANT STRAINS IN APPLE PACKINGHOUSES IN THE UNITED STATES. THIS REDUCES THEIR UTILITY AS CONTROL OPTIONS IN STORAGE SINCE FUNGICIDE FAILURE IS MORE LIKELY TO OCCUR. CONSIDERING CONSUMERS DEMAND APPLES WITH LESS PESTICIDE RESIDUES AND COMMERCIAL APPLE CULTIVARS LACK RESISTANCE TO MOST OF THE POSTHARVEST PATHOGENS NEW INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OPTIONS ARE NECESSARY.POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASE RESEARCH HAS BEEN LIMITED TO WASHINGTON AND OREGON, DEMONSTRATING STORAGE BINS, DUMP TANK WATER, AND THE AIR OF THE PACKINGHOUSE FACILITIES AND COLD ROOMS HARBOR HIGH LEVELS OF ROT PATHOGENS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO POSTHARVEST DECAY, WITH PENICILLIUM SPP. AS THE PREDOMINANT FUNGUS. TO ERADICATE PATHOGENS, TREATING BIN SURFACES WITH STEAM, CLEANING PACKINGHOUSE WALLS AND FLOORS WITH DISINFECTANTS, AND MAINTAINING PROPER CHLORINE LEVELS IN SIZING FLUMES HAVE BEEN RECOMMENDED. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE WESTERN U.S. RESEARCH AND MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS CAN BE EXTRAPOLATED TO MEET THE NEEDS FOR MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS, WHO PRODUCE APPROXIMATELY 760 MILLION POUNDS OF APPLES ANNUALLY. CONSEQUENTLY, THESE PRACTICES ARE NOT ROUTINELY IMPLEMENTED IN APPLE PACKINGHOUSES LOCATED IN THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION DUE TO THE ECONOMIC COST AND THE LACK OF REGION-SPECIFIC RESEARCH DEMONSTRATING THEIR EFFICACY ONREDUCING THE INCIDENCE AND SEVERITY OF POSTHARVEST ROTS. THERE IS AN EXPRESSED NEED FOR RESEARCH AND OPTIMIZED POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING ALTERNATIVES TO SYNTHETIC POSTHARVEST FUNGICIDES, GEARED TOWARDS MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO FILL A MAJOR GAP IN KNOWLEDGE FOR POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASES AND APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR THE MID-ATLANTIC. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS BY IDENTIFYNG THE FUNGI CAUSING POSTHARVEST APPLE ROTS IN PENNSYLVANIA AND MARYLAND PACKINGHOUSES AND DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF WHERE THE FUNGAL SPORES ORIGINATE. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONCURRENTLY BE EVALUATING THE STATUS OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANCE AMONG THE FUNGAL PATHOGENS COLLECTED AGAINST THE FOUR POSTHARVEST FUNGICIDES USED. STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE IF WOODEN AND PLASTIC BINS SERVE AS A VIABLE PATHOGEN SOURCE FOR ROTS, AS DESCRIBED IN WESTERN APPLE PACKHOUSES. CURRENT METHODS, SUCH AS STEAM, AND NEW TOOLS AND DELIVERY SYSTEMS, SUCH AS FOGGING, AND ORGANIC CONTROLS WILL BE EVALUATED FOR SANITIZING BINS AND/OR OTHER SURFACES, AS WELL AS USED TO LIMIT POSTHARVEST APPLE DECAY. SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION WILL BE COMMUNICATED TO STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH EXTENSION PROGRAMMING BOTH IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH FOR OPTIMIZED CHEMICAL AND CULTURAL POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT PROTOCOLS. RESULTS FROM THIS PROJECT ARE EXPECTED TO BE TRANSFORMATIVE AND IMPACTFUL TO MANY APPLE PRODUCING AREAS HAVING SIMILAR PRODUCTION PRACTICES SUCH AS NEW ENGLAND, NEW YORK, MICHIGAN, THE MIDWEST, AND SOUTHEAST REGIONS. THROUGH THE METHODS DESCRIBED, THE ULTIMATE GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE UNDERSTANDING THE STATUS OF POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASES AND DEVELOPING TAILORED, COST-EFFECTIVE, SUSTAINABLE DISEASE MANAGEMENT FOR CONVENTIONAL AND ORGANIC MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS. ADOPTION OF OPTIMIZED POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES WILL BE ECONOMICAL FOR THE STAKEHOLDERS RESULTING IN LESS CROP LOSS WHILE REDUCING HUMAN HEALTH RISKS THROUGH LIMITING EXPOSURE OF FRUIT CONTAMINATED WITH MYCOTOXINS AND MYCOTOXIN-PRODUCING FUNGI.

ARIZONA IS CHARACTERIZED BY EXTREMELY PRODUCTIVE IRRIGATED AGRICULTURAL LANDS, UNIQUE FLORA AND FAUNA, EXTREME AND SENSITIVE ENVIRONMENTS, AND LARGE URBAN CENTERS MADE-UP OF TRANSPLANTED PEOPLE AND CULTURES. OUR DIVERSE STAKEHOLDERS REQUIRE INFORMATION ON THE SAFE AND EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT OF PESTS INCLUDING WAYS TO REDUCE RISKS TO HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT WHILE SUSTAINING ECONOMICALLY VIABLE INDUSTRY IN OUR STATE. AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA, WE HAVE LIMITED AND SHRINKING HUMAN AND FISCAL RESOURCES AVAILABLE TO ADDRESS THESE NEEDS. THE ARIZONA PEST MANAGEMENT CENTER (APMC), FORMED IN RESPONSE TO STAKEHOLDERS' DEMANDS FOR GREATER TRANSPARENCY, ENGAGEMENT AND RELEVANCE, ENCOMPASSES THE FULL SET OF UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA RESEARCH AND EXTENSION RESOURCES INVOLVED IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF IPM IN ARIZONA. THIS REORGANIZATION OF IPM EFFORTS HAS IMPROVED OUR CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY AND ADDRESS STAKEHOLDER IPM NEEDS ACROSS ALL EMPHASIS AREAS, AND TO DOCUMENT OUTCOMES AND IMPACTS. WE SUPPORT IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN AGRICULTURAL, NATURAL AND URBAN ENVIRONMENTS AND SYSTEMATICALLY MEASURE THE ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF OUR PROGRAMS. THE APMC PROVIDES PROVEN SUPPORT FOR STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT, NEEDS ASSESSMENT, STRATEGIC PLANNING, OUTREACH AND EVALUATION OF IPM IN ALL OUR SYSTEMS. IT IS A STRUCTURE THAT BOTH OUR FACULTY AND PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS HAVE EMBRACED.OUR OVERALL GOAL IS TO SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE OUR CAPACITY TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT AND EVALUATE HIGH-IMPACT IPM PROGRAMS CONSISTENT WITH STAKEHOLDER-IDENTIFIED PRIORITIES IN THE FOLLOWING PRIORITY AREAS: IPM IMPLEMENTATION FOR AGRONOMIC CROPS, IPM IMPLEMENTATION FOR SPECIALTY CROPS, IPM IN PUBLIC HEALTH AND IPM TRAINING AND IMPLEMENTATION IN SCHOOLS. THE GOAL OF OUR IPM PROGRAMS IS TO SUPPORT AND ADVANCE IPM IMPLEMENTATION BY END-USERS IN ARIZONA THROUGH A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO EDUCATION AND OUTREACH THAT EMPOWERS PEST MANAGERS TO PUT IPM KNOWLEDGE INTO PRACTICE, RESULTING IN MEASURABLE REDUCTIONS IN ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND HUMAN HEALTH RISKS FROM PESTS AND PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN THESE DIVERSE ENVIRONMENTS. WE ACCOMPLISH THIS THROUGH APPLIED RESEARCH FUNDED THROUGH LEVERAGED RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT AND DISSEMINATION OF EDUCATIONAL OUTPUTS, AS COORDINATED BY LEADERSHIP TEAMS IN EACH EMPHASIS AREA. WE MEASURE CHANGES IN KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICE AND IMPACTS OF IPM THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS AND IMPACT MEASURES AND A DEDICATED IPM ASSESSMENT LEADERSHIP TEAM. THE EXPECTED IMPACT OF OUR OVERALL EFFORTS IS INCREASED IMPLEMENTATION OF IPM IN ALL PRIORITY AREAS AND A REDUCTION IN ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND HUMAN HEALTH RISKS AS A RESULT. ECONOMIC BENEFITS ARE REALIZED BY GROWERS, WHO HELP SUSTAIN SAFE, ABUNDANT AND AFFORDABLE FOOD AND FIBER SUPPLIES, WITH RIPPLING ECONOMIC BENEFITS TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY. ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS INCLUDE EXPECTED REDUCTIONS IN USE OF BROAD-SPECTRUM PESTICIDES, INCREASED DIVERSITY AND FUNCTION OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES INCLUDING SUPPORT FOR POLLINATOR SAFETY. HUMAN HEALTH IMPACTS ARE REALIZED BY LOWERING POTENTIAL EXPOSURES TO HIGHER RISK PESTICIDES AND ALSO BY REDUCING POPULATIONS OF PUBLIC HEALTH PESTS THROUGH APPLIED RESEARCH, EXTENSION AND OUTREACH.

IDAHO INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM (IPM-EIP) RESPONDS TO CLIENTELE NEEDS IDENTIFIED BY STATEWIDE SURVEYS, REGIONAL ADVISORY BOARDS, OUR PRIORITY AREA AND UI PRIORITY EXTENSION TEAMS, AND PEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIC PLANS. positiveFlows.title: THIS IS AN EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM (EIP) PROJECT. DR. CLIFFORD SADOF SERVES AS THE PURDUE IPM COORDINATOR AND DR. WILLIAM JOHNSON IS CO-PROJECT DIRECTOR WITH DEPARTMENTS OF BOTANY AND PLANT PATHOLOGY, AND HORTICULTURE. positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** FALL ARMYWORM (FAW, SPODOPTERA FRUGIPERDA) IS A DEVASTATING INSECT FOR WORLDWIDE CORN PRODUCTION AND FOR OTHER CROP AND NON-CROP PLANT SPECIES. FAW LARVAE FEED ON CORN LEAVES AND EARS CAUSING SEVERE PLANT DAMAGE. FEEDING ON TASSELS DURING WHIRL STAGES (BEFORE TASSEL EMERGENCE) CAN DESTROY TASSELS AND LEAD TO POOR SEED SETTING. FEEDING ON EARS CAN ELEVATE THE LEVEL OF AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN CONTAMINATION. INSECTICIDE CONTROL OF FAW MUST BE SWIFT AND TIMELY. HOST PLANT RESISTANCE IS THE MOST EFFECTIVE CONTROL MECHANISM AND CAN BE ACHIEVED THROUGH THE INTEGRATED USE OF BT GENES AND NATIVE RESISTANCE. BT GENES HAVE BEEN EXTREMELY EFFECTIVE IN CONTROLLING FAW, BUT FAW RESISTANCE TO BT CORN HAS RECENTLY BEEN REPORTED AND IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE AND INCREASE. IN BRAZIL, IT TOOK ONLY THREE YEARS FOR FAW TO BECOME RESISTANT TO MOST COMMERCIALLY RELEASED BT CORN HYBRIDS, EVEN WITH MULTIPLE BT GENES. ANOTHER CONTROL ALTERNATIVE IS TO USE NATIVE RESISTANCE (I.E., NON-BT, BUT NATURALLY EXISTING GENES IN CULTIVATED CORN AND ITS WILD RELATIVES). IT HAS BEEN REPORTED THAT MOST TEMPERATE CORN GERMPLASMS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO FAW, AND SOME TROPICAL CORN GERMPLASMS ARE RESISTANT TO FAW AND CORN EARWORM (HELICOVERPA ZEA). THE CO-PD DR. WENWEI XU HAS SPENT OVER 10 YEARS INVESTIGATING AND UTILIZING THE NATIVE RESISTANCE GENES FROM WILD SPECIES SUCH AS TRIPSACUM (OR GAMMA GRASS) AND TEOSINTE SPECIES. HE HAS DEVELOPED A SET OF INBRED LINES FROM BREEDING CROSSES BETWEEN CORN AND TRIPSACUM. IN PAST FEW YEARS, WE EVALUATED THESE LINES UNDER HEAVY NATURAL FAW INFESTATION PRESSURE IN LUBBOCK AND PUERTO RICO. RESULTS SHOWED THAT SEVERAL OF THE HUNDREDS OF EVALUATED TRIP-LINES WERE HIGHLY RESISTANT TO FAW AND ARE HIGH-YIELDING HYBRIDS. TESTING FOR THE SIX COMMERCIALLY USED BT PROTEINS (CRY1AB, CRY1F, VIP3 AND CRY2A, CRY3B, AND CRY34) DID NOT DETECT THE PRESENCE OF ANY OF THESE SIX BT PROTEINS IN THESE TRIP-LINES, INDICATING THAT THE FAW RESISTANCE IN THE TRIP-LINES IS CONFERRED BY NATIVE GENES.AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN ARE TOXINS THAT CAN BE CARCINOGENIC AND ARE ELEVATED BY DROUGHT AND HEAT STRESS, AND INSECT-FEEDING DAMAGE TO EARS. DROUGHT AND HIGH TEMPERATURES (HEAT STRESS) ARE PREVALENT IN THE SOUTHERN STATES WHICH EXACERBATES THE PREHARVEST MYCOTOXIN ACCUMULATION. THE BREEDING EFFORTS BY THE SEED INDUSTRY ARE FOCUSED IN THE MIDWEST CORN BELT STATES AND VERY LIMITED IN THE SOUTHERN STATES. DAMAGE TO CORN EARS FROM FAW INCREASES THE KERNEL FUNGAL INFECTION AND ACCUMULATION OF AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN. AFLATOXIN CONTAMINATION IS A CHRONIC PROBLEM IN SOUTHERN U.S. CORN PRODUCTION. FUMONISIN HAS BECOME A PROBLEM IN RECENT YEARS. CORN GRAIN THAT HAS HIGH AFLATOXIN OR FUMONISIN CONTAMINATION CANNOT BE USED FOR ANIMAL FEED AND MAY NOT BE SUITABLE FOR ETHANOL PRODUCTION. THE TOXINS ARE MUCH HIGHER IN THE CO-PRODUCTS (I.E., DRIED DISTILLER'S GRAINS), MAKING THEM NOT SUITABLE FOR ANIMAL FEED.THE CORN INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) STRATEGY IN THE PAST 30 YEARS HAS CENTERED AR,OUND BT TECHNOLOGY WITH SUPPLEMENTAL APPLICATION OF INSECTICIDES AND THERE HAS BEEN LIMITED INVESTMENT IN NATIVE RESISTANCE. GENES FROM WILD RELATIVE TRIPSACUM CAN BROADEN THE GENETIC BASIS OF CURRENT U.S. CORN PRODUCTION AND ADD THE NATIVE RESISTANCE TO INSECTS AND DISEASES THAT ARE OTHERWISE ABSENT IN THE CULTIVATED CORN GERMPLASM POOL. WE BELIEVE THAT NATIVE RESISTANCE CAN BOOST THE EFFICACY OF PEST CONTROL FROM BT GENES AND EXTEND THE LIFESPAN OF THE BT TECHNOLOGY. THIS PROJECT WILL VALIDATE OUR HYPOTHESIS AND PRODUCE A NEW AND IMPROVED IPM STRATEGY FROM CURRENTLY BT-CENTERED IPM TO PROLONGED OPTIMAL IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE CORN PRODUCTION. IT WILL LEAD US TO THE NEXT PHASE OF OUR LONG-TERM GOAL - ELUCIDATE THE GENETIC AND PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF NATIVE RESISTANCE FROM THE WILD RELATIVE SPECIES TRIPSACUM, IDENTIFY DNA MARKERS ASSOCIATED WITH NATIVE RESISTANCE GENES, AND TRANSFER THE RESISTANCE TO OTHER ELITE LINES FOR BROADER RESISTANCE APPLICATION.AN EFFECTIVE IPM STRATEGY FOR CORN MUST CONSIDER THE OVERALL ECONOMICS OF THE PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE. IN TEXAS AND OTHER ADJOINING SOUTHWESTERN STATES, CURRENT LOW COMMODITY PRICES, REDUCED IRRIGATION WATER AVAILABILITY, AND INCREASED INPUT COSTS COMPLICATE THE PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE. DECLINING WATER AVAILABILITY FROM THE OGALLALA AQUIFER HAS CONSTRAINED THE CURRENT CORN PRODUCTION IN THIS REGION. ADDRESSING THE REDUCED WATER AVAILABILITY, ENTIRE CORN PRODUCTION SYSTEM MUST ALTER MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO ADDRESS THE REDUCED WATER AVAILABILITY. FURTHERMORE, PAUCITY OF INFORMATION EXISTS ON FAW FEEDING PREFERENCE AND DAMAGE SEVERITY UNDER WATER-STRESSED CONDITIONS. CORN CANNOT EFFECTIVELY BE PRODUCED WITHOUT SUPPLEMENTING AT LEAST 60% EVAPOTRANSPIRATION (ET) OF THE WELL-WATERED PRODUCTION REGIME. DESPITE PROGRESS TOWARDS A MORE INTEGRATED CROSS-DISCIPLINARY APPROACH IN FARMING ENTERPRISES, AGRICULTURE STILL OPERATES IN A COMPARTMENTALIZED MANNER SUCH THAT PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE DONE SEPARATELY FROM CROP PRODUCTION, AND ECONOMICS OF INTEGRATED CROPPING SYSTEMS ARE NOT WELL-DEFINED. CONSEQUENTLY, MOST PRODUCERS DO NOT POSSESS THE NECESSARY DECISION-SUPPORT TOOLS FOR ECONOMICALLY PROFITABLE INPUT USE IN THEIR OVERALL CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. UNDER THESE CIRCUMSTANCES, PROTECTING AND IMPROVING OUR CURRENT TECHNOLOGY BECOMES A NECESSARY FIRST STEP IN ACHIEVING SUSTAINABILITY IN THE CORN PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE.THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THREE CRITICALLY IMPORTANT PROBLEMS: 1) CHARACTERIZE THE EXPRESSION OF NATIVE RESISTANCE FROM THE WILD SPECIES TRIPSACUM AGAINST FAW AND POSSIBLY OTHER LEPIDOPTERAN PESTS (E.G., CORN EARWORM) AND QUANTIFY IF NATIVE RESISTANCE TO INSECTS CAN LEAD TO LOWER AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN ACCUMULATION IN GRAIN, 2) QUANTIFY THE PERFORMANCE AND ADDITIVE VALUE OF NATIVE RESISTANCE AND EXISTING BT TRAITS ACROSS THE RANGE OF WATER-DEFICIT PRODUCTION CONDITIONS, AND 3) DEVELOP SPECIFIC CORN PRODUCTION OPTIMIZATION MODELS THAT MAXIMIZE THE NET RETURNS FROM FAW AND AFLATOXIN-FUMONISIN MAN,AGEMENT UNDER VARIOUS WATER-DEFICIT CROP PRODUCTION CONDITIONS, WHICH WILL EMPOWER PRODUCERS TO OPTIMIZE THE INPUT RESOURCES TO SUSTAIN PROFITABLE CORN PRODUCTION.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** WASHINGTON AND OREGON GROW NEARLY $700 MILLION WORTH OF SWEET CHERRIES ANNUALLY, OR 80% OF THE SWEET CHERRIES PRODUCED IN THE US, ALONG WITH NECTARINES AND PEACHES. HOWEVER, PACIFIC NORTHWEST STONE FRUIT ORCHARDS ARE CURRENTLY EXPERIENCING AN X-DISEASE EPIDEMIC THAT THREATENS PRODUCTION. THE EPIDEMIC IS LEADING TO REMOVAL OF ENTIRE ORCHARD BLOCKS, AND PREVALENCE IS INCREASING RAPIDLY IN THE REGION. THERE IS NO TREATMENT FOR X-DISEASE, AND MANAGEMENT OPTIONS INCLUDE REMOVING INFECTED TREES AND CONTROLLING VECTORS. UNFORTUNATELY, DUE TO A PAUCITY OF RESEARCH IN THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST OVER THE LAST SIXTY YEARS SINCE THE PREVIOUS OUTBREAK IN THE REGION, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THESE VECTORS. THE KEY LEAFHOPPER VECTORS ARE TYPICALLY PRESENT IN ORCHARDS FROM APRIL THROUGH OCTOBER, BUILDING IN ABUNDANCE OVER THE SEASON. THIS PERIOD OF ABUNDANCE HAS APPROXIMATELY DOUBLED THE TIME INTERVAL OVER WHICH INSECT CONTROLS ARE APPLIED. BLOCKS ARE OFTEN TREATED IN 1 TO 3 WEEK INTERVALS AFTER MID-SUMMER HARVEST, OR WHENEVER LEAFHOPPERS ARE FOUND ON TRAPS, RESULTING IN HIGH SCOUTING AND SPRAY COSTS WITH LOW ACCURACY. BECAUSE PHYTOPLASMA TITERS IN PLANTS INCREASE OVER THE COURSE OF THE SEASON, LEAFHOPPER ACQUISITION AND TRANSMISSION LIKELIHOOD ALSO INCREASE, BUT THE TIMING OF PHYTOPLASMA PREVALENCE AND VECTOR ABUNDANCE IS CURRENTLY UNCLEAR. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP PHENOLOGY MODELS FOR PHYTOPLASMA ACQUISITION AND TRANSMISSION IN VECTORS. WE WILL INTEGRATE THESE MODELS WITH ABUNDANCE MODELS TO IMPROVE SPRAY TIMINGS AND OPTIMIZE DISEASE MANAGEMENT.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** IN RECENT 15 YEARS, FREQUENT WARM AND WET WEATHER IN SPRING ALLOWED EPIDEMICS OF FIRE BLIGHT THAT CAUSED LOSSES OF UP TO $22 MILLION PER YEAR IN PEAR AND APPLE. PARTICULARLY IMPACTED WERE PACIFIC NORTHWEST, MID-ATLANTIC AND NORTHEASTERN US INDUSTRIES. BESIDES FRUIT LOSSES FROM FLOWER INFECTIONS, FIRE BLIGHT CANKERS WHICH ARE INFECTED DEAD ZONES ON WOOD BARK, CAN KILL TREES BY TRUNK OR ROOTSTOCK GIRDLING AND CAUSE UP TO 50% LOSSES OF ORCHARD ACREAGE. IF ANTIBIOTICS AREN'T APPLIED TO PROTECT FLOWERS, BLOSSOM BLIGHT INFECTIONS QUICKLY LEAD TO SHOOT BLIGHT INFECTIONS, WHICH THEN LEAD TO DEVELOPMENT OF CANKERS. ALTHOUGH MANY ALTERNATIVES HAVE BEEN TRIED, GROWERS STILL USE COPPER IN SPRING THAT IS NOT ALWAYS EFFECTIVE, ANTIBIOTICS THAT ARE PRONE TO RESISTANCE, AND LABOR-INTENSIVE PRUNING REMOVAL OF SYMPTOMS AS THE MAIN STRATEGY TO CONTROL FIRE BLIGHT. THIS PROJECT'S GOALS ARE TO DEVELOP EFFECTIVE DORMANT COPPER SPRAY TREATMENTS IN MIX WITH BARK PENETRATING OILS FOR ERADICATION OF FIRE BLIGHT BACTERIUM ERWINIA AMYLOVORA IN FIRE BLIGHT CANKERS, EVALUATE SPRAY PROGRAMS WITH DIFFERENT PLANT ACTIVATORS THAT PREVENT SHOOT BLIGHT AND FIRE BLIGHT CANKERS, AND TEST NEWLY DESIGNED ANTIMICROBIAL ENZYMES THAT DEGRADE BIOFILM OF E. AMYLOVORA TO CONTROL BLOSSOM AND SHOOT BLIGHT. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE GROWERS WITH CRITICALLY NEEDED NEXT GENERATION OF CONTROL OPTIONS FOR ALL FIRE BLIGHT PHASES - CANKERS, BLOSSOM BLIGHT, AND SHOOT BLIGHT. THE GOAL OF OUR IPM PROGRAMS IS TO SUPPORT AND ADVANCE IPM IMPLEMENTATION BY END-USERS IN ARIZONA THROUGH A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO EDUCATION AND OUTREACH THAT EMPOWERS PEST MANAGERS TO PUT IPM KNOWLEDGE INTO PRACTICE, RESULTING IN MEASURABLE REDUCTIONS IN ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND HUMAN HEALTH RISKS FROM PESTS AND PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN THESE DIVERSE ENVIRONMENTS. WE ACCOMPLISH THIS THROUGH APPLIED RESEARCH FUNDED THROUGH LEVERAGED RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT AND DISSEMINATION OF EDUCATIONAL OUTPUTS, AS COORDINATED BY LEADERSHIP TEAMS IN EACH EMPHASIS AREA. negativeFlows.title: EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT OF THE STABLE FLY, STOMOXYS CALCITRANS (L.), HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AS A CRITICAL NEED FOR CATTLE PRODUCTION IN THE GREAT PLAINS AND ACROSS THE US. HOWEVER, FLY CONTROL IN PASTURES AND RANGE IS DIFFICULT BECAUSE FLIES ARRIVE FROM DISTRIBUTED SOURCES, FEW REGISTERED INSECTICIDES ARE AVAILABLE, WEEKLY OR PERIODIC RETREATMENTS ARE NEEDED, AND BECAUSE OF DOCUMENTED OR SUSPECTED RESISTANCE TO THE AVAILABLE INSECTICIDES. TOGETHER, THESE FACTORS MAKE FLY MANAGEMENT AND PROTECTION OF PROFITABLE CATTLE PRODUCTION DIFFICULT AND THREATEN PROFITABILITY. THUS, ALTERNATIVE DELIVERY METHODS AND INSECTICIDES SUCH AS NATURAL PRODUCT BIOPESTICIDES (ATTRACTANTS AND REPELLENTS) ARE NEEDED. WE PROPOSE A MULTI-TACTIC IPM SYSTEM EMPLOYING A PUSH-PULL DESIGN IN LARGE PASTURES COMMON TO THE GREAT PLAINS AND OTHER LOCATIONS. A PUSH TREATMENT OF A BOTANICALLY DERIVED REPELLENT BIOPESTICIDE WILL BE USED TO REDUCE ON-ANIMAL FLY NUMBERS AND INCREASE ANIMAL COMFORT AND WELLBEING. TWO TYPES OF TRAPS TARGETING DIFFERENT FLY BEHAVIORS WILL BE USED TO REDUCE AMBIENT STABLE FLY NUMBERS. VISUAL CUES COMBINED WITH ATTRACTIVE ODORS WILL BE USED TO ATTRACT HOST SEEKING STABLE FLIES. THE SECOND TRAP TYPE WILL LURE STABLE FLIES MOVING TO RESTING SITES. BOTH TRAPS WILL INCORPORATE KILL TECHNOLOGIES, STICKY TRAPS IN THE FIRST CASE AND INSECTICIDE IMPREGNATED SUBSTRATE IN THE SECOND. IN ADDITION, TO EVALUATING FLY POPULATION LEVELS, WE WILL MEASURE FREQUENCY OF CATTLE DEFENSIVE BEHAVIORS TO ASSESS THE VALUE OF THE PUSH-PULL DESIGN IN PROTECTING PRODUCTION PROFITABILITY. EXTENSION OUTPUTS WILL INCLUDE AN ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF THE PUSH-PULL STRATEGY.
