positiveFlows.title: SOYBEANS ARE AN IMPORTANT CROP IN THE U.S. HOWEVER, DISEASES CAUSED BY FUNGI SUCH AS DIAPORTHE SPECIES CAN COMPROMISE SOYBEAN SEED QUALITY, AND MANAGING THESE DISEASES IS DIFFICULT BECAUSE NO SOYBEAN VARIETIES WITH COMPLETE RESISTANCE ARE AVAILABLE. WHILE PLANTING SOYBEANS EARLY CAN BOOST YIELDS, RESEARCH IN THE MIDWEST AND SOUTHEASTERN U.S. SHOWS THAT EARLY PLANTING MAY INCREASE SEED DECAY CAUSED BY DIAPORTHE. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IMPROVE SOYBEAN PRODUCTION BY DEVELOPING INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) STRATEGIES THAT REDUCE THE NEED FOR FOLIAR FUNGICIDES. FIELD TRIALS CONDUCTED OVER TWO YEARS AT MULTIPLE SITES IN IOWA AND NORTH DAKOTA WILL STUDY HOW PLANTING DATE, HARVEST TIMING, POST-HARVEST HANDLING, AND FUNGICIDE APPLICATIONS AFFECT SOYBEAN YIELD, SEED QUALITY, AND DIAPORTHE INFECTION -- INCLUDING FUNGICIDE-RESISTANT STRAINS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO EVALUATE THE RETURN ON INVESTMENT (ROI) OF THESE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES BY COMPARING COSTS (SUCH AS FUNGICIDES AND LABOR) TO BENEFITS LIKE INCREASED SEED YIELD, LOWER DISEASE INCIDENCE, AND HIGHER SEED MARKET VALUE. THE RESEARCH WILL ALSO EXPLORE FARMER CONCERNS AND BARRIERS TO ADOPTING THESE STRATEGIES. EXTENSION MATERIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED TO SHAREIPM GUIDANCE ON MANAGING DIAPORTHE AND IMPROVING SEED QUALITY WITH FARMERS AND AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS AT THE STATE, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL LEVELS THROUGH ESTABLISHED EXTENSION PROGRAMS.

FUNGAL FOLIAR DISEASES ARE A GROWING THREAT TO IMPORTANT CROPS LIKE CORN, SOYBEANS, AND POTATOES. THESE DISEASES REDUCE CROP YIELDS, INCREASE PRODUCTION COSTS, AND DRIVE FARMERS TO RELY HEAVILY ON FUNGICIDES. MANY FUNGICIDE SPRAYS ARE APPLIED BASED ON CROP GROWTH STAGE RATHER THAN ACTUAL DISEASE RISK, WHICH CAN RESULT IN UNNECESSARY APPLICATIONS, INCREASED COSTS, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF FUNGICIDE-RESISTANT PATHOGEN STRAINS. FINDING IMPROVED, MORE SUSTAINABLE WAYS TO MANAGE FOLIAR DISEASES IS ESSENTIAL FOR PROTECTING BOTH AGRICULTURE AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY. THIS PROJECT WILL COMBINE LOW-COST AIR SAMPLING DEVICES, CELLULAR WEATHER-MONITORING STATIONS, AND MODERN DNA SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGY TO TRACK DISEASE-CAUSING ORGANISMS IN THE AIR IN CROP FIELDS. BY COLLECTING AIR SAMPLES, MONITORING LOCAL WEATHER CONDITIONS, ANALYZING THE DIVERSITY AND ABUNDANCE OF PLANT PATHOGENS, AND ASSESSING DISEASE INCIDENCE AND SEVERITY, WE WILL BUILD NEW FORECASTING TOOLS THAT CAN PREDICT WHEN AND WHERE DISEASES ARE MOST LIKELY TO OCCUR. THESE TOOLS WILL BE TESTED WITH FARMERS IN VIRGINIA AND OKLAHOMA, SHARED THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND FIELD DEMONSTRATIONS, AND DEVELOPED INTO USER-FRIENDLY WEB AND MOBILE APPLICATIONS THAT PROVIDE REAL-TIME GUIDANCE ON WHEN FUNGICIDE APPLICATIONS ARE TRULY NEEDED.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** AGRICULTURE IS VIRGINIA'S LARGEST PRIVATE INDUSTRY, ADDING APPROXIMATELY $82.3 BILLION ANNUALLY TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY AND PROVIDING MORE THAN 381,800 JOBS. THE STATE'S AGRICULTURAL COMMODITY MIX IS ONE OF THE MOST DIVERSE IN THE NATION. MAJOR COMMODITY SECTORS ADDRESSED IN THIS PROPOSAL INCLUDE BOTH AGRONOMIC AND SPECIALTY CROPS, WHICH WHEN COMBINED COMPRISE ONE-THIRD OF VIRGINIA'S FARM CASH RECEIPTS. DESPITE THE VALUE AND GROWTH OF THESE COMMODITY SECTORS, SIGNIFICANT PEST MANAGEMENT CHALLENGES THREATEN THE PROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF VIRGINIA AGRICULTURE. PROBLEMS WITH A DIVERSE AND EVER-CHANGING ARRAY OF NATIVE AND INVASIVE PEST SPECIES POSE A CONTINUING CHALLENGE, AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ARE NEEDED TO SHIFT GROWERS AWAY FROM PROPHYLACTIC USE OF PESTICIDES AND TOWARD ADOPTION OF IPM. IN ADDITION, IMPROVING THE HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF MANAGED AND WILD POLLINATOR POPULATIONS AND THEIR POLLINATION SERVICES IS ANOTHER INCREASING PRIORITY IN VIRGINIA. DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF COORDINATED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TARGETING YOUTH, BEEKEEPERS, PRODUCERS, AND PESTICIDE APPLICATORS IS NEEDED TO ENSURE THAT GOOD STEWARDSHIP PRACTICES ARE FOLLOWED AND RESPONSIBLE PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE IMPLEMENTED TO PRESERVE POLLINATOR HEALTH. negativeFlows.title: ACCEPTABLE WEED CONTROL IN PLASTICULTURE VEGETABLE SYSTEMS CAN BE DIFFICULT. HERBICIDES ARE RELIED UPON HEAVILY FOR WEED CONTROL; HOWEVER, FEWER PRODUCTS ARE AVAILABLE IN VEGETABLE PRODUCTION COMPARED TO ROW CROPS SUCH AS CORN AND SOYBEAN. IN ADDITION, MANY WEED SPECIES HAVE DEVELOPED RESISTANCE TO THE FEW HERBICIDES AVAILABLE. NON-CHEMICAL OPTIONS, SUCH AS CULTIVATION AND HAND WEEDING CAN BE USED, BUT THESE CAN HAVE INCREASED ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL COSTS. THIS CAN RESULT IN A NEGATIVE IMPACT ON THE OVERALL SUSTAINABILITY OF PLASTICULTURE CROPPING SYSTEMS.COVER CROPS ARE AN ALTERNATIVE WEED MANAGEMENT TOOL THAT HAS BEEN SUCCESSFULLY USED IN MULTIPLE CROPPING SYSTEMS. THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE THE UTILITY OF GRASS COVER CROPS PLANTED IN-BETWEEN ROWS OF PLASTIC CAN BE INTEGRATED WITH OTHER TACTICS FOR ACHIEVING ACCEPTABLE LEVELS OF WEED CONTROL. THE RESULTS OF THIS RESEARCH WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT METHODS FOR WEED CONTROL, WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF WEED MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS AND INCREASE PROFITABILITY IN VEGETABLE PRODUCTION SYSTEMS.

IN ADDITION, INSECTS, SUCH AS MOSQUITOES AND TICKS, AND THEIR VECTOR-BORNE DISEASES ARE PRESENT IN MISSISSIPPI AND THREATEN PUBLIC AND ANIMAL HEALTH, AND INSECTS, SUCH AS FIRE ANTS AND TERMITES, THAT OCCUR IN MISSISSIPPI AFFECT THE LIVES, HOMES, LANDSCAPES, AND COMMUNITIES OF MISSISSIPPI'S CITIZENS. MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY SPECIALISTS MAINTAIN COMPREHENSIVE, MULTIDISCIPLINARY EXTENSION INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) EDUCATION PROGRAMS IN AGRONOMIC CROPS, COMMUNITIES, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND SPECIALTY CROPS AS WELL AS PLANTDISEASE DIAGNOSTIC AND INSECT IDENTIFICATION FACILITIES FOR AGRICULTURAL AND HORTICULTURAL CROPS; THEY WORK TO MONITOR PEST OUTBREAKS AND EPIDEMICS, EVALUATE AND/OR DEVELOP NEW PEST MANAGEMENT METHODS, AND EDUCATE STAKEHOLDERS ON PESTS AND EFFECTIVE IPM PRACTICES WHILE STRIVING TO PROMOTE, IMPLEMENT, AND DEMONSTRATE THE VALUE OF IPM TO STAKEHOLDERS SO STAKEHOLDERS CAN EFFECTIVELY MANAGE PESTS IN WAYS THAT ARE SAFE, EFFECTIVE, AFFORDABLE, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND.THE GOAL OF THE "MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY EXTENSION IPM IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM, 2021-2024" PROJECT IS TO DISSEMINATE IPM INFORMATION AND INCREASE STAKEHOLDER KNOWLEDGE AND IPM IMPLEMENTATION TO HELP MISSISSIPPI'S STAKEHOLDERS EFFECTIVELY MANAGE PESTS, INCLUDING INSECTS, PLANT PATHOGENS/DISEASES, AND WEEDS, THAT AFFECT THEIR LIVES, PROPERTY, OR PRODUCED CROPS/COMMODITIES IN A MANNER THAT MINIMIZES 1) YIELD OR PROPERTY LOSSES, ADVERSE IMPACTS TO HUMAN/ANIMAL HEALTH, AND OTHER ADVERSE PEST-INDUCED EFFECTS, 2) PEST MANAGEMENT COSTS, AND 3) ADVERSE IMPACTS OF IPM STRATEGIES, INCLUDING PESTICIDE USE, TO HUMANS, NON-TARGET ORGANISMS, AND THE ENVIRONMENT IN AGRONOMIC CROPS, COMMUNITIES, SPECIATLTY CROPS, AND PUBLIC HEALTH WITH THE SUPPORT OF PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES. PROJECT COLLABORATORS WITH EXPERTISE IN ENTOMOLOGY, PLANT PATHOLOGY, AND WEED SCIENCE, AND/OR IN THE DESIGNATED PRIORITY AREAS WILL 1) PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND TROUBLESHOOTING TO STAKEHOLDERS; 2) DEVELOP NEW AND MAINTAIN/UPDATE EXISTING TRADITIONAL AND MODERN EDUCATIONAL IPM RESOURCES FOR PESTS, KEY CROPS, AND/OR PRODUCTION SITES THROUGH MULTIPLE DELIVERY METHODS; 3) DEVELOP AND DELIVER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO STAKEHOLDERS; AND 4) CONDUCT SURVEYS, TRIALS, AND DEMONSTRATIONS TO IDENTIFY AND ASSESS TARGET PESTS AND THEIR POPULATIONS/OCCURRENCES IN MS AND TEST/DEMONSTRATE EXPERIMENTAL/RECOMMENDED IPM STRATEGIES. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES THAT WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND TROUBLESHOOTING TO STAKEHOLDERS INCLUDE DIAGNOSTICS BY SPECIALISTS AND/OR DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES, IN-PERSON OR PHONE/ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION WITH CLIENTELE, AND SITE VISITS. EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES DEVELOPED AS PART OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE TRADITIONAL (IN-PRINT) AND VIRTUAL/ONLINE CONTENT INCLUDING EXTENSION PUBLICATIONS, COMPUTER-GENERATED PRESENTATIONS, VIDEOS, NEWSLETTERS, BLOGS, POPULAR PRESS ARTICLES, FIELD DAYS, WORKSHOPS, AND SHORT COURSES, BASED ON KNOWLEDGE GAINED FROM FIELD SURVEYS, TRIALS, AND DEMONSTRATIONS, PUBLISHED SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, AND ATTENDANCE OF SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS WHERE RESEARCH IS SHARED AND DISCUSSED.

MICHIGAN AGRICULTURE IS EXCEPTIONALLY DIVERSE AND CRUCIAL TO THE ECONOMY. MICHIGAN BOASTS MORE THAN 300 COMMODITIES CONTRIBUTING AN ESTIMATED $104 BILLION DOLLARS TO THE STATE'S ECONOMY ANNUALLY. THE AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM ACCOUNTS FOR AN ESTIMATED 805,000 JOBS, REPRESENTING MORE THAN 20% OF THE STATE'S WORKFORCE. MICHIGAN FARMS AND THEIR ECONOMIC OUTPUT ARE AT RISK FROM RAPIDLY EVOLVING PEST CHALLENGES INCLUDING INVASIVE PESTS, CLIMATE CHANGE, CONSUMER PERCEPTIONS, PESTICIDE RESISTANCE, AND REGULATORY CHALLENGES. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT RESPOND TO IPM PRIORITIES IDENTIFIED BY MICHIGAN PRACTITIONERS, GUIDED BY A STAKEHOLDER ALLIANCE AND PRIORITIZED BY THE IPM ROADMAP. IT ADDRESSES THE CPPM FOCUS AREAS OF PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS AND IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES. THIS IS AN EXTENSION-LED EFFORT TO INCREASE AGRICULTURE AND COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDER AWARENESS, KNOWLEDGE AND ADOPTION OF IPM PRACTICES AND TOOLS THROUGH TRADITIONAL AND NOVEL OUTREACH EFFORTS. IT ALSO SUPPORTS CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RELATED TO POLLINATOR HEALTH. OUR PROGRAM'S PROVEN INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORTS THE IMPACTFUL OUTREACH OF DOZENS OF EXTENSION EDUCATORS AND SPECIALISTS WHOSE EFFORTS ARE OPTIMIZED BY A STRATEGIC COORDINATION AND COMMUNICATION PLAN WITH NATIONAL REACH. RESOURCES WILL BE SHARED BROADLY THROUGH MULTI-STATE COLLABORATIONS, REGIONAL COALITIONS AND THE MSU EXTENSION OUTREACH NETWORK.

THIS IS AN EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT (EIP). THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO REDUCE THE RATE OF PEST ESTABLISHMENT ON ALASKA'S FARMS AND RANCHES. OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) INCREASE THE TRAINING AND SUPPORT OF IPM ASSISTANTS SO THEY CAN AID IN EARLY DETECTION AND RAPID RESPONSE TO PESTS IN COMMUNITIES AND SPECIALTY CROPS, ESPECIALLY NON-NATIVE PESTS, 2) ENGAGE AND EDUCATE PRODUCERS ABOUT POLLINATOR HEALTH AND PESTICIDE RISKS WITH RESEARCH CONDUCTED IN COMMERCIAL PEONIES AND REVEGETATION PROJECTS IN AGRICULTURAL SETTINGS, 3) CONDUCT A PILOT PROJECT USING SMART PRECISION DRONE TECHNOLOGY TO IDENTIFY, TREAT, AND MONITOR WEEDS IN ALASKA'S DIVERSE AGRICULTURAL ENVIRONMENTS, AND 4) EXPAND AND IMPROVE IPM ONLINE DISTANCE TRAINING COURSES FOR PESTICIDE APPLICATORS (RECERTIFICATION CONTINUING EDUCATION) INCLUDING ON-LINE SHORT COURSES FOR SMALL-SCALE PRODUCERS, HOME GARDENERS, AND MASTER GARDENERS. BASED ON THE 2017 CENSUS OF AGRICULTURE, ALASKA LED THE NATION IN THE PERCENT INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF FARMS, HAD THE HIGHEST PERCENTAGE OF NEW AND BEGINNING FARMERS, HAD THE SECOND YOUNGEST AVERAGE AGE OF PRODUCERS, AND WAS NUMBER TWO IN THE PERCENTAGE OF FEMALE PRODUCERS OR IN THE PERCENTAGE OF PRODUCERS WITH MILITARY SERVICE. MANY OF THESE NEW PRODUCERS ARE UNAWARE OF PESTS OR ALASKA-BASED IPM TECHNIQUES. THESE CONDITIONS INCREASE THE RISK THAT NEW PESTS COULD BE INTRODUCED OR ESTABLISHED HERE IN ALASKA. IN ALL, OUR PRIMARY PRIORITIES ARE IPM IMPLEMENTATIONS IN SPECIALTY CROPS (37%), COMMUNITIES (44%), AND POLLINATOR HEALTH (13%).OUR SECONDARY PRIORITY IS IPM EDUCATION FOR PESTICIDE APPLICATORS (6%).

BRETZIELLA FAGACEARUM IS A FUNGAL PLANT PATHOGEN THAT CAUSES OAK WILT DISEASE IN MANY ECOLOGICALLY AND ECONOMICALLY IMPORTANT OAK TREE SPECIES. SYMPTOMS OF OAK WILT ARE EASILY CONFUSED WITH DROUGHT STRESS AND OTHER BACTERIAL DISEASES THAT ARE VECTORED BY INSECT LEAFHOPPERS. EFFORTS TO MAP U.S. OCCURRENCE AND DISTRIBUTION OF OAK WILT HAVE BEEN COMPLICATED BY THE SIMILAR APPEARANCE OF CONSEQUENCES TO OAK OF THESE DIFFERENT BIOTIC AND ABIOTIC STRESSORS. IN THE URBAN LANDSCAPE AND NURSERY, INACCURATE DISEASE DIAGNOSIS CAN LEAD TO OVER-RELIANCE ON CHEMICAL PESTICIDES AND USE OF INEFFECTIVE TREATMENTS APPLIED TO CONTROL THE WRONG PROBLEM. THIS CONFUSION ALSO HAS RESULTED IN COMPLICATIONS FOR U.S. AGRICULTURE AND EXPORT COMMODITIES. HARVESTED LOGS INTENDED FOR INTERNATIONAL EXPORT ARE SUBJECT TO QUARANTINE WHEN ORIGINATING FROM LOCATIONS WITHIN THE U.S. WHERE OAK WILT IS DOCUMENTED. LOGS FROM THESE AREAS MUST BE PROVIDED PHYTOSANITARY TREATMENTS IN ORDER FOR EXPORT TO PROCEED. PENDING WITHDRAWAL OF THE PHYTOSANITARY FUMIGANT METHYL BROMIDE POTENTIALLY WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF ACCESS TO SOME EUROPEAN AND ASIAN MARKETS FOR AGROFORESTRY OAK LOGS.THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO THE HOST PLANT GENES THAT ARE ACTIVATED ACROSS TIME, AS A NATURAL METHOD OF HOST PLANT DEFENSE IN WHITE OAK AND RED OAK TREE SEEDLINGS, WHEN SUBJECTED TO INFECTION BY WITH THE OAK WILT PATHOGEN. EFFORTS WILL ALSO DOCUMENT THE GENES UP-REGULATED WITHIN A MOST VIRULENT AND A LEAST VIRULENT ISOLATE OF THE FUNGAL PATHOGEN WHEN ATTACKING TWO OAK HOST SPECIES, AS THE PATHOGEN SEEKS TO OVERCOME THE HOST PLANT DEFENSES. TAKEN TOGETHER, NEW SCIENCE ARISING FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL PROVIDE NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO HOST PLANT RESISTANCE THAT CAN INFORM FUTURE TREE BREEDING IN OAKS THAT YIELDS GREATER STRENGTH AND SUSTAINABILITY FOR THIS HIGHLY VALUED U.S. FOREST SPECIES AND AGRICULTURAL CROP COMMODITY. LASTLY, THIS RESEARCH COMPLIMENTS THE PARTICIPATING TEAM'S ONGOING EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A RAPID MOLECULAR TEST TO FACILITATE OAK WILT DIAGNOSIS AND DETECTION IN LANDSCAPE TREES, FOREST SPECIMENS, AND HARVESTED LOGS INTENDED FOR INTERNATIONAL EXPORT. IN COMBINATION, THESE APPROACHES ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE POWERFUL NEW TOOLS IN EFFORTS TO DELINEATE REGIONAL OCCURRENCE OF OAK WILT AND TO PREVENT ITS SPREAD INTO NEW, UNINFESTED LOCATIONS AROUND THE GLOBE.

THE DIAMONDBACK MOTH, PLUTELLA XYLOSTELLA, IS A NOTORIOUS PEST OF COLE AND OTHER BRASSICA CROPS. IT IS ALSO KNOWN FOR THE RAPID EVOLUTION OF RESISTANCE TO INSECTICIDES, AND IS LIKELY RESISTANT TO A BROADER ARRAY OF INSECTICIDES THAN ANY OTHER CROP PEST. IN THE SOUTHEASTERN USA, THIS HAS LED TO FREQUENT CONTROL FAILURES AND ASSOCIATED LOSS OF REVENUE FOR GROWERS. IN THE PREVIOUS CYCLE, WE DEVELOPED A MAXIMUM DOSE ASSAY TO ASSIST GROWERS IN PLANNING INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS. THIS ASSAY EXPOSES LARVAE TO THE MAXIMUM LABELED DOSE OF A VARIETY OF INSECTICIDES; IF LARVAE SURVIVE THE EXPOSURE IN SIGNIFICANT NUMBERS USE OF THE INSECTICIDE IS COUNTER-INDICATED. A CONSTRAINT OF THE ASSAY IS THE NEED FOR A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF LARVAE. THE CURRENT STUDY SEEKS TO DEVELOP GENETIC TOOLS, PARTICULARLY QUANTITATIVE PCR ASSAYS, TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE OF ALLELES (OR MUTATIONS) ASSOCIATED WITH RESISTANCE, INITIALLY TO CHLORANTRANILIPROLE (CORAGEN) AND LATER TO OTHER INSECTICIDES. IDEALLY THESE ASSAYSCAN BE RAPID AND WORK WITH SMALLER SAMPLE SIZES OF LARVAE, OR WITH ADULTS CAUGHT ON PHEROMONE TRAPS, PROVIDING TIMELY INFORMATION TO GROWERS PLANNING THEIR INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS.INITIALLY WE WILL FOCUS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC PCR ASSAYS TO QUANTIFY THE PROPORTION OF SUSCEPTIBLE AND RESISTANT ALLELES IN FIELD POPULATIONS. COMPARISON OF THE RESULTS WITH BIOASSAY RESULTS FROM THE SAME POPULATIONS WILL ALLOW US TO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL RELATING ALLELE FREQUENCY TO THE LIKELIHOOD OF CONTROL FAILURE. SUBSEQUENTLY, THE ASSAY WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO GROWERS AND EXTENSION AGENTS TO ASSIST IN PLANNING INSECTICIDE ROTATIONS AND IN MANAGING TO AVOID INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE.ALTHOUGH THE PLANNED DIAGNOSTIC ASSAYS WILL EXPLOIT KNOWN MUTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH RESISTANCE, THERE IS MUCH THAT IS STILL UNCLEAR ABOUT RESISTANCE TO DIAMIDES (AND OTHER CLASSES OF INSECTICIDES FOR THAT MATTER). WE WILL USE HIGH THROUGHPUT MRNA/CDNA SEQUENCING AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS TO STUDY THE RESPONSE TO DIAMIDE (CHLORTRANILIPROLE AND CYANTRANILIPROLE) EXPOSURE IN SUSCEPTIBLE AND RESISTANT POPULATIONS OF DIAMONDBACK MOTHS. THIS APPROACH IS LIKELY TO IDENTIFY MULTIPLE FACTORS INVOLVED IN RESISTANCE, INCLUDING UP-OR DOWN-REGULATION OF SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTS AS WELL AS POTENTIALLY NOVEL MUTATIONS IN TARGET SITES. THIS MORE GLOBAL INDERSTANDING OF THE DIFFERENTIAL RESPONSE OF RESISTANT VS SUSCEPTIBLE POPULATIONS MAY LEAD TO NOVEL APPROACHES TO RESISTANCE MANAGEMENT.

OUR PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO REDUCE HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL RISK FROM PEST MANAGEMENT, IMPROVE IPM PRACTICES AND INCREASE IPM ADOPTION. THE MONTANA STATE UNIVERSITY IPM PROGRAM IS A HIGHLY COLLABORATIVE, ENGAGED, AND EFFECTIVE GROUP. WE HAVE SEVERAL NEW AND CONTINUING PROGRAMS THAT WILL BE EMPHASIZED IN THIS PROJECT THAT ARE DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE CPPM GOALS OF PLANT PROTECTION TACTICS AND TOOLS, ENHANCING AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY, AND IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES. OUR PRIMARY AREAS OF EMPHASIS AREAGRONOMIC CROPS; COMMUNITIES; SPECIALTY CROPS; POLLINATOR HEALTH; PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES; AND PESTICIDE APPLICATORS. EMPHASES AND SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:AGRONOMIC CROPS: REAL TIME MONITORING OF PESTS VIA A WEBSITE AND FARMER COOPERATORS; HANDS-ON TRAINING AND RESEARCH- BASED LEARNING MATERIALS FOR AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS;COMMUNITIES: EXPAND AVAILABILITY AND ACCESSIBILITY OF ONLINE LEARNING RESOURCES; PROVIDE HANDS-ON TRAINING, TOOLKITS AND LEARNING MATERIALS FOR STAKEHOLDERS; PARTICIPATE IN MULTISTATE COOPERATIVE PROJECTS; EARLY DETECTION AND RAPID RESPONSE TO THE BROWN MARMORATED STINK BUG;SPECIALTY CROPS: IMPROVE SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS' KNOWLEDGE AND IMPLEMENTATION OF TIMELY TOOLS FOR PEST MANAGEMENT, HANDS-ON WORKSHOPS AND GROWER GUIDES; POLLINATOR HEALTH: IMPROVE AWARENESS OF POLLINATOR HEALTH AND HABITAT;PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES: EDUCATE CLIENTS OF THE DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY ON IPM-BASED PEST MANAGEMENT OPTIONS; PROVIDE RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS; PESTICIDE APPLICATORS: PROVIDE HANDS-ON TRAINING AND LEARNING MATERIALS FOR PESTICIDE APPLICATORS.

THIS IS AN EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM (EIP) PROJECT. THE OHIO STATE UNIVERSITYEIP PROPOSAL ENCOURAGES COLLABORATION AND INNOVATION BETWEEN SPECIALISTS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS INTHE DEPARTMENTS OF ENTOMOLOGY, EXTENSION AND PLANT PATHOLOGY TO MEET A MULTITUDE OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS FROM RURAL AND URBAN AUDIENCES. WE HAVE ASSEMBLED A BALANCED PRIORITY BASED PROGRAM THAT PROVIDES TRADITIONAL EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES (CONFERENCES, WORKSHOPS, FIELD DAYS) WHILE BEING TECHNOLOGICALLY ADROIT TO CONDUCT VIRTUAL PROGRAMS SHOULD MANDATED SOCIAL AND HEALTH RESTRICTIONS REQUIRE IT. WE EMBRACE THE MULTIPLIER EFFECT OF OUR EXTENSION TEAMS AND UTILIZE WEBSITES, WEBINARS AND INSTRUCTIONAL VIDEOS TO DISTRIBUTE OUR IPM PROGRAMMING.WE WILL CONDUCT PROGRAMS IN SPECIALTY CROPS (31% OF BUDGET) WITH THE GOAL OF IPM IMPLEMENTATION AND ADOPTION ON FRUITS AND VEGETABLES WHILE INCREASING INVASIVE AND KEY PEST AWARENESS AND MONITORING. AGRONOMIC CROPS (20% OF BUDGET) WILL FOCUS ON IPM IMPLEMENTATION AND ADOPTIONON FIELD CROPS FOR TRADITIONAL AND EMERGING PESTS, TRANSGENIC CROPS, AND GRAIN MYCOTOXINS. PUBLIC HEALTH PESTS SUCH AS TICKS AND BED BUGS (12% OF BUDGET) WILL DELIVER IPM TRAINING RELATED TO IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF BED BUGS IN INHABITED STRUCTURES AND TICKS IN URBAN AND RECREATIONAL SPACES THROUGHOUT THE STATE. OUR POLLINATOR HEALTH INITIATIVE (10% OF BUDGET) FOCUS WILL RAISE AWARENESS OF IMPERILED BEES OF ALL TYPES THAT MIGHT BE FOUND IN URBAN LANDSCAPES BY DEVELOPING URBAN LANDSCAPE DESIGNS THAT ARE POLLINATOR FRIENDLY, EASY TO INSTALL AND MAINTAIN. THE PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES (7% OF BUDGET) ARE CORNERSTONE TO IPM AND OFFER ASSISTANCE IN HELPING GROWERS AND CITIZENSBY IDENTIFYING PESTS AND OFFERING RECOMMENDATIONS TO A VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDERS.ALL PROJECTS WILL BE EVALUATED TO MEASURE KNOWLEDGE GAIN AND PRACTICE ADOPTION, PROGRESSING TOWARD THE ULTIMATE GOALS OF INCREASED FOOD PRODUCTION, FOOD SECURITY, AND ADOPTION OF SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIALLY RESPONSIBLE PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES.

THIS PROPOSAL, LED BY DR. GERALD (LEE) MILLER WITH ASSOCIATE DEAN DR. ROBERT KALLENBACH AS LEAD ADMINISTRATIVE CONTACT, IS SUBMITTED TO THE EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM AREA OF THE CPPM PROGRAM. SINCE 1980, MU HAS SUSTAINED AN EXTENSIVE IPM OUTREACH PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTED BY A WIDELY UTILIZED WEBSITE WHICH HOUSES A STATEWIDE INSECT MONITORING PROGRAM ALONG WITH NUMEROUS NEWSLETTERS, VIDEOS, AND PRINT PUBLICATIONS. MAIN ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE IPM IN AGRONOMIC CROPS PRIORITY AREA (75%) INCLUDE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LONG-TERM DEMONSTRATION PLOT TO EVALUATE THE INFLUENCE OF WEED MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES ON SOIL HEALTH, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STATE-WIDE ASSESSMENT PLAN FOR PLANT DISEASE OUTBREAKS AND SWEEP NET INSECT CAPTURES. IN ADDITION, MISSOURI IPM STANDS TO COLLABORATE IN REGIONAL INITIATIVES SUCH AS CROP SCOUTING SCHOOLS, THE GREAT LAKES VEGETABLE WORKING GROUP, AND A REGIONAL INSECT MONITORING NETWORK. THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH AND DIVERSE OBJECTIVES WILL ENHANCE AWARENESS AND ACCEPTANCE OF IPM PRACTICES IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN AREAS.

PROGRAM PRIORITIES AND OBJECTIVES REFLECT THE DOCUMENTED NEEDS OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS AND ARE CENTERED ON THE NIFA CPPM PROGRAM LOGIC MODEL. THESE PROGRAMS ARE DESCRIBED UNDER PRIORITY HEADINGS AND ADDRESS THE NATIONAL IPM ROADMAP GOALS OF IMPROVED COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS, REDUCED HEALTH RISKS AND MINIMIZED ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF PEST MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS.PRIMARY PRIORITY: IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN COMMUNITIES (42% OF PROGRAMMING), FOCUSING ON LANDSCAPE IPM, WHICH ADDRESSES THE NEEDS OF HOMEOWNERS, LANDSCAPERS AND GROWERS THROUGH EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AND SITE VISITS. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO INFORM OUR STAKEHOLDERS OF PEST ISSUES AND IPM TECHNIQUES FOR NEW AND EXISTING PESTS.PRIMARY PRIORITY: IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN SPECIALTY CROPS (48% OF PROGRAMMING). EXOTIC FRUIT, VEGETABLE AND NURSERY PESTS REQUIRE NOVEL IPM METHODS AND NEW GROWERS NEED SPECIAL ATTENTION. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO PROVIDE GROWERS WITH KNOWLEDGE OF IPM TECHNIQUES FOR EMERGING PESTS AND ASSISTANCE IN PEST MANAGEMENT DECISION MAKING.SECONDARY PRIORITY: IPM SUPPORT FOR PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES (10% OF PROGRAMMING). PROPER PEST IDENTIFICATION IS ESSENTIAL FOR OPTIMIZING BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. OUR PLANT PROTECTION CLINIC SERVES COMMERCIAL GROWERS, LAND MANAGERS, HOMEOWNERS AND STATE AND FEDERAL REGULATORY OFFICIALS. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO IDENTIFY PLANT PESTS FOR INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS INVOLVED IN PEST MANAGEMENT. PROPER DIAGNOSIS GUIDES OUR IPM PROGRAMMING.

THIS ARDP RESEARCH-LED PROPOSAL WITH EXTENSION ADDRESSING CPPM FOCUS AREA (A) PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS. WE AIM AT DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING EASY TO ADOPT, ECONOMICALLY VIABLE, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY APPROPRIATE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE JOINT MANAGEMENT BROMUS TECTORUM (CHEATGRASS, DOWNY BROME) AND FUSARIUM CROWN ROT, AN INTERACTING PEST COMPLEX THREATENING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF SMALL GRAIN CROPS. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, WE WILL: (1) ASSESS THE INDIVIDUAL AND INTERACTIVE EFFECTS OF COMMONLY USED PRACTICES ON THE JOINT MANAGEMENT OF B. TECTORUM AND FUSARIUM CROWN ROT IN WHEAT SYSTEMS, (2) APPRAISE ECONOMIC TRADE-OFFS IN THE JOINT MANAGEMENT OF B. TECTORUM AND FUSARIUM, (3) PRODUCE A DECISION MANAGEMENT TOOL TO MODEL THE RELATIVE IMPORTANCE OF FERTILIZATION, FUNGICIDE USE, AND FUSARIUM CROWN ROT ON B. TECTORUM POPULATION GROWTH, WHEAT YIELD, QUALITY, AND ECONOMIC RETURNS, AND (4) DEVELOP AND DELIVER EDUCATION AND EXTENSION MATERIAL ON THE INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF B. TECTORUM AND FUSARIUM CROWN ROT IN SMALL GRAIN SYSTEMS. THE RELEVANCE OF THIS SYSTEMS-ORIENTED PROJECT IS UNDERSCORED BY: (A) THE SELECTION OF B. TECTORUM BIOTYPES RESISTANT TO DIFFERENT HERBICIDE GROUPS, (B) THE IMPACTS THAT B. TECTORUM AND FUSARIUM HAVE ON SMALL GRAIN SYSTEMS, (C) THE ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS OCCURRING BETWEEN THESE TWO PEST GROUPS, AND (D) THE MANAGEMENT CONTRADICTIONS THAT EMERGE FROM SINGLE PEST MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS. THE ECOLOGICALLY-BASED PRINCIPLES DEVELOPED IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALLOW AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS ACROSS THE SEMI-ARID ENVIRONMENTS OF THE NORTHERN GREAT PLAINS TO DEVELOP INTEGRATED PATHOGEN AND WEEDS MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS WHICH, IN TURN, WILL ENHANCE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF RURAL COMMUNITIES.

ROW CROP IPMAR GROWERS RELY ON RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION TO HELP THEM USE CONTEMPORARY IPM STRATEGIES: USE OF TRANSGENIC CROPS; ECONOMIC THRESHOLDS; CULTURAL PRACTICES; DIAGNOSIS AND SCOUT-ING; AND DELAYING INSECT AND WEED RESISTANCE TO PESTICIDES. THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE AGRONOMIC CROP IPM PROGRAM IS TO PARTNER EXTENSION & RESEARCH FACULTY WITH COUNTY EDUCATORS TO DEVELOP AND DELIVER THIS INFORMATION TO GROWERS CONSULTANTS AND INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES. THE AR IPMPROGRAM SENDS WEEKLY UPDATES TO COUNTY IPM EDUCATORS AND CONSULTANTS VIA PODCASTS ELECTRONIC NEWSLETTERS IMAGES OF INSECTS WEEDS AND DISEASE SYMPTOMS TO ALERT GROWERS STATEWIDE. IPM FACULTY USE SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS AND THE AR CROPS BLOG TO REACH STAKEHOLDERS QUICKLY AND INCREASE EXCHANGE AMONG USERS.ANIMAL IPMCATTLE AND POULTRY ARE THE TOP LIVESTOCK COMMODITIES IN AR. AR IS HOME TO APPROXIMATELY 26000 CATTLE OPERATIONS OF WHICH 24000 OPERATORS HAD <100 HEAD OF CATTLE. AR CATTLE GROWERS AND POULTRY INTEGRATORS RELY ON RESEARCH-BASED IPM INFORMATION AND STRATEGIES WHETHER TO CONTROL PESTS DIRECTLY ON CATTLE PESTS OF PASTURE ORPOULTRY PESTS. THE ANIMAL IPM PROGRAM PARTNERS EXTENSION AND RESEARCH FACULTY WITH COUNTY AGENTS TO DEVELOP AND DELIVER INFORMATION TO GROWERS CONSULTANTS AND INDUSTRY. EVALUATIONS COMPARING FLY MANAGEMENT METHODS THAT INCORPORATE SURVEILLANCE MONITORING INSECTICIDE CLASS ROTATION AND ECONOMIC THRESHOLDS INTO FLY MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS ARE APPROPRIATE COUNTY MINI-GRANT PROJECTS. INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE IMPROPER TIMING ON INSECTICIDE EAR TAG APPLICA-TION AND LACK OF INSECTICIDE CLASS ROTATION ROUTINELY RESULT IN CONTROL FAILURES. INSECTICIDAL EAR TAGS INSECTICIDE SPRAYS INSECTICIDE SELF-TREATMENT DEVICES OR FEED-THROUGH INSECT GROWTH REGULATORS ARE THE MOST COMMON METHODS. OTHER METHODS ARE APPROPRIATE FOR PRODUCERS DESIRING ALTERNATIVES. PREVIOUS RESEARCH IN AR HAS SHOWN UP TO 70% HORN FLY CONTROL WITH THE BRUCE (1940) TRAP ANDHAS EVALUATED AN EFFECTIVE FATTY ACID BASED INSECTICIDE SUITABLE FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTION. BOVINE ANAPLASMOSIS IS A SIGNIFICANT CONCERN FOR AR CATTLE PRODUCERS. ANAPLASMA MARGINALEIS WIDESPREAD IN AR BEEF HERDS WITH ONE RECENT STUDY FINDING A SEROPREVALENCE RATE OF OVER 58%. IN THE REGION WITH THE HIGHEST PREVALENCE ALMOST 94% OF TESTED CATTLE WERE POSITIVE AND IN THE REGIONS WITH THE LOWEST PREVALENCE THERE WAS >36% SEROPOSITIVITY. DEMONSTRATION OF EFFECTIVE TICK CONTROL AND INCREASED AWARENESS OF TICK MANAGEMENT TO REDUCE ANAPLASMOSIS INCIDENCE IS AN IMPORTANT COMPONENT OF AR' IPM PROGRAM. IN ADDITION THE INVASIVE ASIAN LONGHORNED TICK (HAEMAPHYSALIS LONGICORNIS) HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED IN AR. EFFORTS TO CONTINUE SURVEILLANCE OF THIS NEW LIVESTOCK PEST ARE NEEDED. INSECTICIDES A RE EFFECTIVE IN PROVIDING CONTROL HOWEVER LIKE BSM DAMAGE SOME PRODUCERS ARE UNAWARE THAT CHINCH BUGS CAUSE THE DAMAGE.SPECIALTY CROP IPMSPECIALTY CROP PRODUCTION IS AN IMPORTANT PART OF AR'S STATE ECONOMY AND ADD DIVERSITY TO THE AGRICULTURE OF THE STATE.PRODUCTION OF SPECIALTY CROPS HAS INCREASED SINCE 2017 DUE TO INTEREST IN LOCALLY GROWN PRODUCE. negativeFlows.title: AGRICULTURE IS MD'S LARGEST INDUSTRY, EMPLOYING ~ 350,000 PEOPLE AND CONTRIBUTING $8.25 BILLION ANNUALLY TO THE ECONOMY; AND THE CHESAPEAKE BAY IS THE SECOND MOST IMPORTANT ECONOMIC RESOURCE IN MD. THIS SITUATION MAKES CREATING ECO-FRIENDLY IPM PROGRAMS IN MD ESSENTIAL. TO PROTECT THE BAY, FARMERS MUST LEARN RESPONSIVE IPM PRACTICES. UMES'S SMALL FARM PROGRAM (SFP) IS TASKED WITH DIRECTING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT IMPROVE THE ECONOMIC CONDITION OF SMALL-SCALE, LIMITED-RESOURCE AND/OR SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS, ALLOWING THEM TO OVERCOME THEIR CHALLENGES AND ENABLE THEM TO FARM SUSTAINABLY. HOWEVER, UMES'S ABILITY TO OFFER FARMERS IPM INSTRUCTION IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY ARDUOUS AS SFP'S FUNDS ARE NOT LINKED TO IPM TRAINING. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO HELP CROP AND POULTRY FARMERS MOVE FORWARD IN ADOPTING PRACTICES THAT PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH AND ARE ECO-FRIENDLY AND ECONOMICALLY EFFICIENT. TO THIS END, WE WILL BROADEN AND DIVERSIFY OUR INVOLVEMENT IN IPM DEVELOPMENT, DELIVERY, AND IMPLEMENTATION BY FORMING A STRONGER PARTNERSHIP WITH FARMERS. THESE EFFORTS WILL STRENGTHEN OUR ABILITY TO: I) DISSEMINATE NEW RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION TO END-USERS, II) REACH A GREATER NUMBER OF STAKEHOLDERS, III) ELIMINATE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT LOWER FARM PROFITS, AND IV) ENHANCE CLIENTELE CONFIDENCE IN IMPLEMENTING NOVEL IPM TOOLS THAT SUPPORT THE NATIONAL ROADMAP FOR IPM. FOR THIS EIP PROJECT, WE ALLOCATED 50% OF THE BUDGET FOR THE PROJECT PROPOSAL'S PRIMARY PRIORITY AREA: THE IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN SPECIALTY CROPS OF THIS PROJECT, FOCUSING ON CUCURBITS, STRAWBERRY, AND GRAPE. WE ALLOCATED 23% AND 17% OF THE BUDGET TO THE IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN AGRONOMIC CROPS (SOYBEAN AND HEMP) AND IPM IMPLEMENTATION IN ANIMAL AGRICULTURE FOCUSING ON POULTRY. ?

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** IN 2022, THE U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY REVOKED ALL AGRICULTURAL REGISTRATIONS OF CHLORPYRIFOS. BECAUSE OF THESE REGULATORY DECISIONS, SWEETPOTATO GROWERS LOST THEIR MOST IMPORTANT INSECTICIDE TO COMBAT SOIL INSECT LOSSES. THIS CHANGE HAS DRIVEN AN INDUSTRY-WIDE SHIFT FROM CHLORPYRIFOS TO PRE-PLANT SPRAYS OF BIFENTHRIN (PYRETHROID) COMBINED WITH NEONICOTINOIDS. THESE APPLICATIONS ARE FOLLOWED BY WITH 2-3 BIFENTHRIN APPLICATIONS TO CONTROL ANNUAL WIREWORM SPECIES DURING THE GROWING SEASON. DESPITE MAXIMIZING PROPHYLACTIC BIFENTHRIN USE, GROWERS EXPERIENCED GREATER THAN EXPECTED SWEETPOTATO LOSSES IN 2022. THE LOSS OF CHLORPYRIFOS REPRESENTS A TIMELY OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE IPM STRATEGIES FOR SOIL INSECT MANAGEMENT IN SWEETPOTATO. INFORMATION DEVELOPED BY THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY LOCATIONS AT RISK FOR INFESTATION AND DAMAGE BASED ON THE LANDSCAPE SURROUNDING TARGET FIELDS. WE WILL LEVERAGE MONITORING TOOLS TO TEST DIFFERENT INSECTICIDE TIMINGS AND DELIVERIES TO HELP REDUCE PEST LOSSES IN THE ABSENCE OF CHLORPYRIFOS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** APPLES ARE ONE OF THE TOPMOST CONSUMED FRUIT IN THE UNITED STATES, SECOND IN POPULARITY ONLY TO BANANAS. THEY HAVE AN ANNUAL FARM-GATE VALUE OF NEARLY US$4 BILLION, WITH DOWNSTREAM REVENUES EXCEEDING US$15 BILLION. APPLES ARE AVAILABLE AND ENJOYED YEAR-ROUND BECAUSE THEY CAN BE HELD IN COLD STORAGE UNDER CONTROLLED ATMOSPHERE CONDITIONS, WHICH SUSPENDS THE RIPENING PROCESS SUCH THAT AN APPLE MAINTAINS ITS CRISPNESS AND TASTE 9-11 MONTHS AFTER THEY WERE HARVESTED. POSTHARVEST ROT DURING STORAGE CAUSED BY FUNGAL PATHOGENS IS A PERSISTENT THREAT TO THE GLOBAL US APPLE INDUSTRY. THIS NOT ONLY REDUCES THEIR QUALITY, INCREASES FOOD LOSS, BUT ALSO CAN LEAD TO MYCOTOXIN CONTAMINATION OF PROCESSED FRUIT PRODUCTS. ANNUAL LOSSES DUE TO POSTHARVEST ROTS RANGE BETWEEN 1%-15% IN THE UNITED STATES, ALONE. CURRENT ESTIMATES OF THE ECONOMIC LOSSES DUE TO POSTHARVEST APPLE ROTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE; HOWEVER, ESTIMATING 15% LOSS OF THE 4.5-5 MILLION TONNES OF APPLES PRODUCED ANNUALLY IN THE UNITED STATES, AND AN AVERAGE PRICE OF US$1.5 PER POUND, UP TO US$2.5 BILLION ARE LOST EACH YEAR DUE TO POSTHARVEST ROTS. APPROXIMATELY A DOZEN DISEASES CAN AFFECT APPLES DURING STORAGE. THE MOST FREQUENT POSTHARVEST ROTS OF APPLES ARE BLUE MOLD, CAUSED BY PENICILLIUM EXPANSUM AND OTHER PENICILLIUM SPP., AND GRAY MOLD, CAUSED BY BOTRYTIS CINEREA. THE FUNGI CAUSING BLUE MOLD ARE OF MOST CONCERN SINCE SEVERAL OF THE SPECIES PRODUCE THE MYCOTOXIN PATULIN. UNFORTUNATELY, NO APPLE VARIETIES EXIST THAT ARE RESISTANT TO THESE DISEASES AND MANAGEMENT OPTIONS OF POSTHARVEST APPLE ROT ARE LIMITED. GROWERS RELY ON CONTINUED USE OF SYNTHETIC FUNGICIDES, WHICH THERE ARE FEW AND HAVE CAUSED THE EMERGENCE OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANT STRAINS IN APPLE PACKINGHOUSES IN THE UNITED STATES. THIS REDUCES THEIR UTILITY AS CONTROL OPTIONS IN STORAGE SINCE FUNGICIDE FAILURE IS MORE LIKELY TO OCCUR. CONSIDERING CONSUMERS DEMAND APPLES WITH LESS PESTICIDE RESIDUES AND COMMERCIAL APPLE CULTIVARS LACK RESISTANCE TO MOST OF THE POSTHARVEST PATHOGENS NEW INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OPTIONS ARE NECESSARY.POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASE RESEARCH HAS BEEN LIMITED TO WASHINGTON AND OREGON, DEMONSTRATING STORAGE BINS, DUMP TANK WATER, AND THE AIR OF THE PACKINGHOUSE FACILITIES AND COLD ROOMS HARBOR HIGH LEVELS OF ROT PATHOGENS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO POSTHARVEST DECAY, WITH PENICILLIUM SPP. AS THE PREDOMINANT FUNGUS. TO ERADICATE PATHOGENS, TREATING BIN SURFACES WITH STEAM, CLEANING PACKINGHOUSE WALLS AND FLOORS WITH DISINFECTANTS, AND MAINTAINING PROPER CHLORINE LEVELS IN SIZING FLUMES HAVE BEEN RECOMMENDED. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE WESTERN U.S. RESEARCH AND MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS CAN BE EXTRAPOLATED TO MEET THE NEEDS FOR MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS, WHO PRODUCE APPROXIMATELY 760 MILLION POUNDS OF APPLES ANNUALLY. CONSEQUENTLY, THESE PRACTICES ARE NOT ROUTINELY IMPLEMENTED IN APPLE PACKINGHOUSES LOCATED IN THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION DUE TO THE ECONOMIC COST AND THE LACK OF REGION-SPECIFIC RESEARCH DEMONSTRATING THEIR EFFICACY ONREDUCING THE INCIDENCE AND SEVERITY OF POSTHARVEST ROTS. THERE IS AN EXPRESSED NEED FOR RESEARCH AND OPTIMIZED POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING ALTERNATIVES TO SYNTHETIC POSTHARVEST FUNGICIDES, GEARED TOWARDS MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO FILL A MAJOR GAP IN KNOWLEDGE FOR POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASES AND APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR THE MID-ATLANTIC. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS BY IDENTIFYNG THE FUNGI CAUSING POSTHARVEST APPLE ROTS IN PENNSYLVANIA AND MARYLAND PACKINGHOUSES AND DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF WHERE THE FUNGAL SPORES ORIGINATE. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONCURRENTLY BE EVALUATING THE STATUS OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANCE AMONG THE FUNGAL PATHOGENS COLLECTED AGAINST THE FOUR POSTHARVEST FUNGICIDES USED. STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE IF WOODEN AND PLASTIC BINS SERVE AS A VIABLE PATHOGEN SOURCE FOR ROTS, AS DESCRIBED IN WESTERN APPLE PACKHOUSES. CURRENT METHODS, SUCH AS STEAM, AND NEW TOOLS AND DELIVERY SYSTEMS, SUCH AS FOGGING, AND ORGANIC CONTROLS WILL BE EVALUATED FOR SANITIZING BINS AND/OR OTHER SURFACES, AS WELL AS USED TO LIMIT POSTHARVEST APPLE DECAY. SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION WILL BE COMMUNICATED TO STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH EXTENSION PROGRAMMING BOTH IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH FOR OPTIMIZED CHEMICAL AND CULTURAL POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT PROTOCOLS. RESULTS FROM THIS PROJECT ARE EXPECTED TO BE TRANSFORMATIVE AND IMPACTFUL TO MANY APPLE PRODUCING AREAS HAVING SIMILAR PRODUCTION PRACTICES SUCH AS NEW ENGLAND, NEW YORK, MICHIGAN, THE MIDWEST, AND SOUTHEAST REGIONS. THROUGH THE METHODS DESCRIBED, THE ULTIMATE GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE UNDERSTANDING THE STATUS OF POSTHARVEST APPLE DISEASES AND DEVELOPING TAILORED, COST-EFFECTIVE, SUSTAINABLE DISEASE MANAGEMENT FOR CONVENTIONAL AND ORGANIC MID-ATLANTIC APPLE GROWERS AND PACKERS. ADOPTION OF OPTIMIZED POSTHARVEST DISEASE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES WILL BE ECONOMICAL FOR THE STAKEHOLDERS RESULTING IN LESS CROP LOSS WHILE REDUCING HUMAN HEALTH RISKS THROUGH LIMITING EXPOSURE OF FRUIT CONTAMINATED WITH MYCOTOXINS AND MYCOTOXIN-PRODUCING FUNGI.

MARY CONCKLIN WILL SERVE AS PROGRAM COORDINATOR; DR. MICHAEL O'NEILL IS THE IPM ADMINISTRATIVE CONTACT. IPM TEAM MEMBERS INCLUDE MARY CONCKLIN (FRUIT IPM), VICTORIA WALLACE (SCHOOL IPM, POLLINATOR HEALTH), ROSA RAUDALES (HORTICULTURE/FLORICULTURE IPM), SHURESH GHIMIRE AND ANA LEGRAND (VEGETABLE IPM). AN EVALUATION SPECIALIST AND PLANT DIAGNOSTICIAN ARE BEING HIRED. THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT PROGRAM IS A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT THAT EMPLOYS SUSTAINABLE, SCIENCE-BASED APPROACHES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF PLANT PESTS BY RECOMMENDING METHODS THAT ARE EFFECTIVE, ECONOMICALLY SOUND AND ECOLOGICALLY COMPATIBLE. THE PROPOSED OBJECTIVES WILL DIRECT AND PROMOTE IPM PROGRAM EFFORTS TO MAINTAIN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL AND GREEN INDUSTRY BUSINESSES BY PROVIDING ON-SITE IPM TRAINING AND EDUCATION. IPM TRAINING AND OUTREACH WILL ALSO TARGET SCHOOL GROUNDS MANAGERS, MUNICIPALITIES, AND ALL OTHER CONNECTICUT STAKEHOLDERS. FULFILLMENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN INCREASED AWARENESS AND THE USE OF IPM BY COMMODITY GROUPS, THE PUBLIC, LEGISLATORS, RESEARCHERS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES ALIGN WITH CPPM GOALS OF INCREASED IPM ADOPTION, REDUCED ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS, ECONOMICAL AND IMPROVED IPM PRACTICES, AND REDUCED HUMAN HEALTH RISKS, AS WELL AS THE NATIONAL IPM ROADMAP GOALS TO INCREASE ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFICIENCY OF EFFECTIVE, ECONOMICAL AND SAFE PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, TO DEVELOP NEW PRACTICES, AND TO MITIGATE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF INVASIVE SPECIES. THE UCONN IPM EXTENSION FACULTY PARTICIPATE IN STATE, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL COLLABORATIONS.

THE PURPOSE OF THE DELAWARE EXTENSION IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT IS TO FACILITATE INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) STRATEGY ADOPTION BY DELAWARE STAKEHOLDERS WITH THE OVERALL GOAL OF IMPROVING THE HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF DELAWARE AGRICULTURAL SERVICE PROVIDERS, HORTICULTURAL SERVICE PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITIES. THIS GOAL WILL BE ACHIEVED BY COORDINATING EFFORTS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: AGRONOMIC CROPS, SPECIALTY CROPS, COMMUNITIES, POLLINATOR HEALTH, AS WELL AS SUPPORTING PEST DIAGNOSTIC FACILITIES AND PESTICIDE APPLICATOR EDUCATION. PEST SURVEILLANCE, SURVEYS AND DEMONSTRATION TRIALS IN AGRONOMIC AND SPECIALTY CROPS AS WELL AS LANDSCAPE HORTICULTURAL CROPS ARE JUST SOME OF THE ACTIVITIES IN THIS PROPOSAL THAT ADDRESS PLANT PROTECTION TACTICS AND TOOLS. OUR PROPOSAL WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THE UD PLANT DIAGNOSTIC CLINIC, THEREBY ADDRESSING THE CPPM GOAL OF ENHANCING AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY. ACTIVITIES FOCUSING ON SMALL FARMS, HIGH TUNNELS, AND LANDSCAPE PESTS, AND COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES WITH MASTER GARDENERS ARE SOME OF THE PRIMARY MECHANISMS FOR WHICH THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES. FURTHERMORE, DEMONSTRATIONS OF THE INFLUENCE OF PROPER CULTURAL TECHNIQUES, PEST SURVEILLANCE, AND ADDRESSING TACTICS FOR IMPROVING POLLINATOR HEALTH CONTRIBUTE TO BOTH IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES AND PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE MULTIPLE HERBICIDE-RESISTANT (MHR) WEED EPIDEMIC IS THREATENING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF KEY AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES BY RENDERING VALUABLE HERBICIDES INEFFECTIVE. MHR IS CAUSING REDUCED CROP YIELDS, INCREASED WEED MANAGEMENT COSTS, AND INCREASED RELIANCE ON HERBICIDES WITH GREATER ENVIRONMENTAL PERSISTENCE, WHICH THREATENS A REVERSION TO TILLAGE, NEGATING DECADES OF SOIL HEALTH AND CONSERVATION GAINS. SEED IMPACT MILLS PROCESS AND KILL THE VAST MAJORITY OF WEED SEEDS AS THEY EXIT THE COMBINE DURING CROP HARVEST. THIS NEW TECHNOLOGY IS BEING RAPIDLY AND WIDELY ADOPTED IN AUSTRALIA, WHERE IT IS PROVIDING AN EFFECTIVE INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT TOOL FOR MHR. HOWEVER, WE ARE YET TO FULLY UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THIS SYSTEM UNDER US PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. OUR MULTI-STATE, MULTI-REGION TEAM HAS 12 SEED IMPACT MILLS ON-FARM ACROSS OUR NETWORK, A POSITION ENJOYED BY NO OTHER GROUP. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THIS FARMER COOPERATIVE ON-FARM RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECT ARE TO COMPREHENSIVELY EVALUATE SEED IMPACT MILL EFFICACY FOR ECONOMIC DECISION DRIVER WEEDS IN SOYBEAN AND WHEAT AND COMMUNICATE THESE RESULTS TO GROWERS THROUGH OUR GROW (GETTING RID OF WEEDS) WEBSITE, SOCIAL MEDIA, DEVELOPING EXTENSION BULLETINS, INTERACTIVE WORKSHOPS/FIELD DAYS, AND PEER-TO-PEER LEARNING THROUGH ON-FARM PROGRAMS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL DETERMINE OPERATING COSTS OF SEED IMPACT MILLS AND CREATE A COST CALCULATOR DECISION SUPPORT TOOL FOR USING THIS TECHNOLOGY. WE ANTICIPATE THAT THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE ADOPTION OF SEED IMPACT MILL TECHNOLOGY IN US SOYBEAN AND WHEAT PRODUCTION, REDUCING THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPACT, AND SPREAD OF MHR WEEDS, AND INCREASING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF CROP PRODUCTION.

THE EUROPEAN PEPPER MOTH (EPM) (DUPONCHELIA FOVEALIS) IS A MAJOR, YET LARGELY UNRECOGNIZED EXOTIC INVASIVE INSECT PEST OF NURSERY, VEGETABLE, FRUIT, AND GREENHOUSE CROPS. LARVAL EPM FEED ON FOLIAGE, FRUIT, AND FREQUENTLY ON LOWER STEMS OF PLANTS, CAUSING STEM DIEBACK, PLANT DEATH, AND ECONOMIC LOSS, WITH SEVERAL GROWERS ESTIMATING AN ANNUAL ECONOMIC LOSSGREATER THAN $200,000 FROM EPM. CURRENT MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES ARE INEFFECTIVE, BECAUSE INFORMATION ABOUT EPM DISTRIBUTION, POPULATION CYCLES, PLANT PREFERENCES, AND EFFECTIVE INSECTICIDES IS LACKING. EXTENSION PERSONNEL, GROWERS, THE IR-4 PROJECT, AND TRADE ASSOCIATIONS HAVE RECOGNIZED EPM AS ONE OF THE TOP PRIORITY PESTS THAT NEEDS TO BE ADDRESSED. THIS MULTI-STATE PROJECT (TX AND NC) SPANS ACROSS A LARGE AREA OF THE EPM RANGE, PROVIDING DATA AND INSIGHT RELEVANT TO SOUTHERN USA. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INCREASE ADOPTION OF EFFECTIVE INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) PRACTICES AND DECREASE ECONOMIC LOSS DUE TO EPM BY INVESTIGATING THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: (1) DETERMINE THE DISTRIBUTION AND PHENOLOGY OF EPM; (2) DETERMINE EPM PREFERENCE AND DAMAGE TO NURSERY CROP SPECIES AND CULTIVARS; (3) DETERMINE HOW IRRIGATION AND FERTILIZER PRACTICES CAN INFLUENCE DAMAGE CAUSED BY EPM; AND (4) DETERMINE THE EFFICACY OF STANDARD AND BIOLOGICAL INSECTICIDES TO MANAGE EPM. RESULTS FROM THIS STUDY WILL BE PUBLISHED IN PEER-REVIEWED PAPERS, INDUSTRY MAGAZINES, UNIVERSITY EXTENSION ARTICLES, WEBSITES, AND THROUGH EDDMAPS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** WASHINGTON AND OREGON GROW NEARLY $700 MILLION WORTH OF SWEET CHERRIES ANNUALLY, OR 80% OF THE SWEET CHERRIES PRODUCED IN THE US, ALONG WITH NECTARINES AND PEACHES. HOWEVER, PACIFIC NORTHWEST STONE FRUIT ORCHARDS ARE CURRENTLY EXPERIENCING AN X-DISEASE EPIDEMIC THAT THREATENS PRODUCTION. THE EPIDEMIC IS LEADING TO REMOVAL OF ENTIRE ORCHARD BLOCKS, AND PREVALENCE IS INCREASING RAPIDLY IN THE REGION. THERE IS NO TREATMENT FOR X-DISEASE, AND MANAGEMENT OPTIONS INCLUDE REMOVING INFECTED TREES AND CONTROLLING VECTORS. UNFORTUNATELY, DUE TO A PAUCITY OF RESEARCH IN THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST OVER THE LAST SIXTY YEARS SINCE THE PREVIOUS OUTBREAK IN THE REGION, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THESE VECTORS. THE KEY LEAFHOPPER VECTORS ARE TYPICALLY PRESENT IN ORCHARDS FROM APRIL THROUGH OCTOBER, BUILDING IN ABUNDANCE OVER THE SEASON. THIS PERIOD OF ABUNDANCE HAS APPROXIMATELY DOUBLED THE TIME INTERVAL OVER WHICH INSECT CONTROLS ARE APPLIED. BLOCKS ARE OFTEN TREATED IN 1 TO 3 WEEK INTERVALS AFTER MID-SUMMER HARVEST, OR WHENEVER LEAFHOPPERS ARE FOUND ON TRAPS, RESULTING IN HIGH SCOUTING AND SPRAY COSTS WITH LOW ACCURACY. BECAUSE PHYTOPLASMA TITERS IN PLANTS INCREASE OVER THE COURSE OF THE SEASON, LEAFHOPPER ACQUISITION AND TRANSMISSION LIKELIHOOD ALSO INCREASE, BUT THE TIMING OF PHYTOPLASMA PREVALENCE AND VECTOR ABUNDANCE IS CURRENTLY UNCLEAR. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP PHENOLOGY MODELS FOR PHYTOPLASMA ACQUISITION AND TRANSMISSION IN VECTORS. WE WILL INTEGRATE THESE MODELS WITH ABUNDANCE MODELS TO IMPROVE SPRAY TIMINGS AND OPTIMIZE DISEASE MANAGEMENT.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE CURRENT PROPOSAL IS AN ARDP APPLIED RESEARCH (SINGLE-FUNCTION) PROJECT. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES THE PLANT PROTECTION TOOLS AND TACTICS CPPM FOCUS AREA, WITH EMPHASIS ON CERCOSPORA LEAF BLIGHT (CLB) OF SOYBEAN. SOYBEAN GROWERS IN THE MID-SOUTH HAVE STRUGGLED WITH THE MANAGEMENT OF CLB FOR NEARLY TWO DECADES; CLB EPIDEMIOLOGY WAS UNCLEAR, RESISTANCE IN COMMERCIAL SOYBEAN CULTIVARS WAS LIMITED, FEW FUNGICIDES WERE EFFECTIVE AGAINST THE PATHOGEN, AND RESISTANCE TO COMMONLY USED FUNGICIDES WAS WIDESPREAD. THUS, OVER THE PAST FIVE YEARS, LOSSES DUE TO CLB ACROSS AR, LA, AND MS IS ESTIMATED TO HAVE BEEN >$250 MILLION. RECENTLY, RESEARCH IN THE MID-SOUTH HAS PROVIDED NEW INSIGHTS INTO SOURCES OF CLB INOCULUM, DOCUMENTED SOME RESISTANCE IN COMMERCIAL CULTIVARS, AND IDENTIFIED NEW FUNGICIDES EFFECTIVE AGAINST THE DISEASE. HOWEVER, KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN IN THE INTRICACIES OF CLB EPIDEMIOLOGY, MANAGEMENT OF FUNGICIDE RESISTANCE PROBLEMS, AND INTEGRATION OF ALL AVAILABLE TOOLS TO IMPROVE CLB MANAGEMENT. THIS PROJECT IS A COLLABORATIVE MULTI-STATE EFFORT THAT AIMS TO ADVANCE RESEARCH INSIGHTS GENERATED FROM STAKEHOLDER SUPPORTED PROJECTS AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND AND TARGET CLB MANAGEMENT. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT ARE TO 1) DETERMINE THE IMPORTANCE OF AIR-BORNE CONIDIA IN THE DISEASE CYCLE AND IDENTIFY ENVIRONMENTAL PREDICTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE DEVELOPMENT, 2) DEVELOP TOOLS TO RAPIDLY MONITOR RESISTANCE TO COMMONLY USED FUNGICIDE CHEMISTRIES, AND 3) INTEGRATE IMPROVED FUNGICIDE APPLICATION TIMING AND HOST RESISTANCE IN CLB DISEASE MANAGEMENT. TOGETHER, THE PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE, LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT SOLUTIONS FOR CLB, CRUCIAL TO PROTECT THE $41 BILLION US SOYBEAN CROP.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** FALL ARMYWORM (FAW, SPODOPTERA FRUGIPERDA) IS A DEVASTATING INSECT FOR WORLDWIDE CORN PRODUCTION AND FOR OTHER CROP AND NON-CROP PLANT SPECIES. FAW LARVAE FEED ON CORN LEAVES AND EARS CAUSING SEVERE PLANT DAMAGE. FEEDING ON TASSELS DURING WHIRL STAGES (BEFORE TASSEL EMERGENCE) CAN DESTROY TASSELS AND LEAD TO POOR SEED SETTING. FEEDING ON EARS CAN ELEVATE THE LEVEL OF AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN CONTAMINATION. INSECTICIDE CONTROL OF FAW MUST BE SWIFT AND TIMELY. HOST PLANT RESISTANCE IS THE MOST EFFECTIVE CONTROL MECHANISM AND CAN BE ACHIEVED THROUGH THE INTEGRATED USE OF BT GENES AND NATIVE RESISTANCE. BT GENES HAVE BEEN EXTREMELY EFFECTIVE IN CONTROLLING FAW, BUT FAW RESISTANCE TO BT CORN HAS RECENTLY BEEN REPORTED AND IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE AND INCREASE. IN BRAZIL, IT TOOK ONLY THREE YEARS FOR FAW TO BECOME RESISTANT TO MOST COMMERCIALLY RELEASED BT CORN HYBRIDS, EVEN WITH MULTIPLE BT GENES. ANOTHER CONTROL ALTERNATIVE IS TO USE NATIVE RESISTANCE (I.E., NON-BT, BUT NATURALLY EXISTING GENES IN CULTIVATED CORN AND ITS WILD RELATIVES). IT HAS BEEN REPORTED THAT MOST TEMPERATE CORN GERMPLASMS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO FAW, AND SOME TROPICAL CORN GERMPLASMS ARE RESISTANT TO FAW AND CORN EARWORM (HELICOVERPA ZEA). THE CO-PD DR. WENWEI XU HAS SPENT OVER 10 YEARS INVESTIGATING AND UTILIZING THE NATIVE RESISTANCE GENES FROM WILD SPECIES SUCH AS TRIPSACUM (OR GAMMA GRASS) AND TEOSINTE SPECIES. HE HAS DEVELOPED A SET OF INBRED LINES FROM BREEDING CROSSES BETWEEN CORN AND TRIPSACUM. IN PAST FEW YEARS, WE EVALUATED THESE LINES UNDER HEAVY NATURAL FAW INFESTATION PRESSURE IN LUBBOCK AND PUERTO RICO. RESULTS SHOWED THAT SEVERAL OF THE HUNDREDS OF EVALUATED TRIP-LINES WERE HIGHLY RESISTANT TO FAW AND ARE HIGH-YIELDING HYBRIDS. TESTING FOR THE SIX COMMERCIALLY USED BT PROTEINS (CRY1AB, CRY1F, VIP3 AND CRY2A, CRY3B, AND CRY34) DID NOT DETECT THE PRESENCE OF ANY OF THESE SIX BT PROTEINS IN THESE TRIP-LINES, INDICATING THAT THE FAW RESISTANCE IN THE TRIP-LINES IS CONFERRED BY NATIVE GENES.AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN ARE TOXINS THAT CAN BE CARCINOGENIC AND ARE ELEVATED BY DROUGHT AND HEAT STRESS, AND INSECT-FEEDING DAMAGE TO EARS. DROUGHT AND HIGH TEMPERATURES (HEAT STRESS) ARE PREVALENT IN THE SOUTHERN STATES WHICH EXACERBATES THE PREHARVEST MYCOTOXIN ACCUMULATION. THE BREEDING EFFORTS BY THE SEED INDUSTRY ARE FOCUSED IN THE MIDWEST CORN BELT STATES AND VERY LIMITED IN THE SOUTHERN STATES. DAMAGE TO CORN EARS FROM FAW INCREASES THE KERNEL FUNGAL INFECTION AND ACCUMULATION OF AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN. AFLATOXIN CONTAMINATION IS A CHRONIC PROBLEM IN SOUTHERN U.S. CORN PRODUCTION. FUMONISIN HAS BECOME A PROBLEM IN RECENT YEARS. CORN GRAIN THAT HAS HIGH AFLATOXIN OR FUMONISIN CONTAMINATION CANNOT BE USED FOR ANIMAL FEED AND MAY NOT BE SUITABLE FOR ETHANOL PRODUCTION. THE TOXINS ARE MUCH HIGHER IN THE CO-PRODUCTS (I.E., DRIED DISTILLER'S GRAINS), MAKING THEM NOT SUITABLE FOR ANIMAL FEED.THE CORN INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) STRATEGY IN THE PAST 30 YEARS HAS CENTERED AR,OUND BT TECHNOLOGY WITH SUPPLEMENTAL APPLICATION OF INSECTICIDES AND THERE HAS BEEN LIMITED INVESTMENT IN NATIVE RESISTANCE. GENES FROM WILD RELATIVE TRIPSACUM CAN BROADEN THE GENETIC BASIS OF CURRENT U.S. CORN PRODUCTION AND ADD THE NATIVE RESISTANCE TO INSECTS AND DISEASES THAT ARE OTHERWISE ABSENT IN THE CULTIVATED CORN GERMPLASM POOL. WE BELIEVE THAT NATIVE RESISTANCE CAN BOOST THE EFFICACY OF PEST CONTROL FROM BT GENES AND EXTEND THE LIFESPAN OF THE BT TECHNOLOGY. THIS PROJECT WILL VALIDATE OUR HYPOTHESIS AND PRODUCE A NEW AND IMPROVED IPM STRATEGY FROM CURRENTLY BT-CENTERED IPM TO PROLONGED OPTIMAL IPM FOR SUSTAINABLE CORN PRODUCTION. IT WILL LEAD US TO THE NEXT PHASE OF OUR LONG-TERM GOAL - ELUCIDATE THE GENETIC AND PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF NATIVE RESISTANCE FROM THE WILD RELATIVE SPECIES TRIPSACUM, IDENTIFY DNA MARKERS ASSOCIATED WITH NATIVE RESISTANCE GENES, AND TRANSFER THE RESISTANCE TO OTHER ELITE LINES FOR BROADER RESISTANCE APPLICATION.AN EFFECTIVE IPM STRATEGY FOR CORN MUST CONSIDER THE OVERALL ECONOMICS OF THE PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE. IN TEXAS AND OTHER ADJOINING SOUTHWESTERN STATES, CURRENT LOW COMMODITY PRICES, REDUCED IRRIGATION WATER AVAILABILITY, AND INCREASED INPUT COSTS COMPLICATE THE PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE. DECLINING WATER AVAILABILITY FROM THE OGALLALA AQUIFER HAS CONSTRAINED THE CURRENT CORN PRODUCTION IN THIS REGION. ADDRESSING THE REDUCED WATER AVAILABILITY, ENTIRE CORN PRODUCTION SYSTEM MUST ALTER MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO ADDRESS THE REDUCED WATER AVAILABILITY. FURTHERMORE, PAUCITY OF INFORMATION EXISTS ON FAW FEEDING PREFERENCE AND DAMAGE SEVERITY UNDER WATER-STRESSED CONDITIONS. CORN CANNOT EFFECTIVELY BE PRODUCED WITHOUT SUPPLEMENTING AT LEAST 60% EVAPOTRANSPIRATION (ET) OF THE WELL-WATERED PRODUCTION REGIME. DESPITE PROGRESS TOWARDS A MORE INTEGRATED CROSS-DISCIPLINARY APPROACH IN FARMING ENTERPRISES, AGRICULTURE STILL OPERATES IN A COMPARTMENTALIZED MANNER SUCH THAT PEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE DONE SEPARATELY FROM CROP PRODUCTION, AND ECONOMICS OF INTEGRATED CROPPING SYSTEMS ARE NOT WELL-DEFINED. CONSEQUENTLY, MOST PRODUCERS DO NOT POSSESS THE NECESSARY DECISION-SUPPORT TOOLS FOR ECONOMICALLY PROFITABLE INPUT USE IN THEIR OVERALL CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. UNDER THESE CIRCUMSTANCES, PROTECTING AND IMPROVING OUR CURRENT TECHNOLOGY BECOMES A NECESSARY FIRST STEP IN ACHIEVING SUSTAINABILITY IN THE CORN PRODUCTION ENTERPRISE.THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THREE CRITICALLY IMPORTANT PROBLEMS: 1) CHARACTERIZE THE EXPRESSION OF NATIVE RESISTANCE FROM THE WILD SPECIES TRIPSACUM AGAINST FAW AND POSSIBLY OTHER LEPIDOPTERAN PESTS (E.G., CORN EARWORM) AND QUANTIFY IF NATIVE RESISTANCE TO INSECTS CAN LEAD TO LOWER AFLATOXIN AND FUMONISIN ACCUMULATION IN GRAIN, 2) QUANTIFY THE PERFORMANCE AND ADDITIVE VALUE OF NATIVE RESISTANCE AND EXISTING BT TRAITS ACROSS THE RANGE OF WATER-DEFICIT PRODUCTION CONDITIONS, AND 3) DEVELOP SPECIFIC CORN PRODUCTION OPTIMIZATION MODELS THAT MAXIMIZE THE NET RETURNS FROM FAW AND AFLATOXIN-FUMONISIN MAN,AGEMENT UNDER VARIOUS WATER-DEFICIT CROP PRODUCTION CONDITIONS, WHICH WILL EMPOWER PRODUCERS TO OPTIMIZE THE INPUT RESOURCES TO SUSTAIN PROFITABLE CORN PRODUCTION.
